nahhas-meani:1-1.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱلْحَمْدُ للَّهِ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَجَعَلَ ٱلظُّلُمَاتِ وَٱلنُّورَ﴾.
Qatāda said: Allah created the heaven before the earth, the night before the day, and the Garden before the Fire.
As for His saying ﴿وَالأَرْضَ بَعْدَ ذَلِكَ دَحَاهَا﴾, its meaning is: He spread it out.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ثْمَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, they associate partners (with Him).
Al-Kisāʾī said: One says عَدَلْتُ الشّيءَ بالشّيءِ عُدولاً when you have made it equal to it.
This view comes back to the view of Mujāhid, because when they worship something else along with Allah, they have made it equal to Him and have associated partners.

nahhas-meani:2-2.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُمْ مِّن طِينٍ ثُمَّ قَضَىۤ أَجَلاً وَأَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى عِندَهُ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Khuṣayf and Qatāda said — and this is the wording of al-Ḥasan —: He decreed the term of this world, from the day He created you until you die; ﴿وَأَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى عِندَهُ﴾ means the Hereafter.
﴿ثُمَّ أَنتُمْ تَمْتَرُونَ﴾, that is: you doubt, and worship others along with Him.

nahhas-meani:3-3.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱللَّهُ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَفِي ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
It has been said: the meaning is "and He is a god (إلهٌ) in the heavens and in the earth."
The alif and lām (in الله), according to one of Sībawayh's two views, are a replacement for a hamza, the original form in his view being إلهٌ.
So the meaning on this view is: He is the One worshipped in the heavens and in the earth.
It is also possible that the meaning is: and He is Allah, the One alone in being taken as god in the heavens and in the earth — just as you say: "He is in (seeing to) people's needs, and in prayer."
It is also possible that it is a khabar (predicate) after a khabar, the meaning being: and He is Allah in the heavens, and He is Allah in the earth.

nahhas-meani:6-6.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَلَمْ يَرَوْاْ كَمْ أَهْلَكْنَا مِن قَبْلِهِم مِّن قَرْنٍ﴾.
It has been said: القَرْن is sixty years; and it has been said: seventy; so the implied form (taqdīr) on this view is "of the people of a qarn".
More correct than this view is that القَرْنُ is every (generation of) people in an age, because it is taken from iqtirān (being joined together), i.e. people joined to one another.
In the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ, he said: "The best of people is the qarn in which I am" — meaning his Companions — "then those who follow them, then those who follow them."
Most of the ḥadīth scholars hold that القَرْن is a hundred years, and they argued that the Prophet said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Busr: "You will live a qarn", and he lived a hundred years.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَرْسَلْنَا ٱلسَّمَآءَ عَلَيْهِم مِّدْرَاراً﴾.
That is: pouring down abundantly upon them. مِدْرَارٌ (the mifʿāl pattern) expresses abundance, as one says امرأة مِذْكارٌ (a woman who bears many males) when she often gives birth to males, and مِئْناثٌ (one who bears many females).

nahhas-meani:7-7.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَوْ نَزَّلْنَا عَلَيْكَ كِتَاباً فِي قِرْطَاسٍ فَلَمَسُوهُ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ لَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ إِنْ هَـٰذَآ إِلاَّ سِحْرٌ مُّبِينٌ﴾.
That is: they had set disbelief and obstinacy in their souls, so whenever they saw a sign they said "Sorcery!" — just as they asked for the splitting of the moon, and when it split they said: ﴿هَذَا سِحْرٌ مُسْتَمِرٌّ﴾. Likewise too: if Allah sent down to them a book from the sky, they would say: "This is nothing but manifest sorcery."

nahhas-meani:8-8.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَقَالُواْ لَوْلاۤ أُنزِلَ عَلَيْهِ مَلَكٌ وَلَوْ أَنزَلْنَا مَلَكاً لَّقُضِيَ ٱلأَمْرُ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said, from Mujāhid: that is, the Hour would have come.
The meaning according to the philologists is: their destruction would have been sealed; and this comes back to that (first) view.

nahhas-meani:9-9.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَوْ جَعَلْنَاهُ مَلَكاً لَّجَعَلْنَاهُ رَجُلاً﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, in the form of the children of Ādam.
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَلَبَسْنَا عَلَيْهِم مَّا يَلْبِسُونَ﴾.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He means the People of the Book, because they altered the description of the Prophet ﷺ in their book and disobeyed what they were commanded.
Al-Kisāʾī said: One says لَبَسْتُ عليهم الأمرَ، أَلْبِسُهُ لَبْساً when you have confused it, i.e. made it obscure.

nahhas-meani:10-10.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَحَاقَ بِٱلَّذِينَ سَخِرُواْ مِنْهُمْ مَّا كَانُواْ بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِءُونَ﴾.
الحَيْقُ in the language is the harm of a person's own deed that comes back upon him; and from it is: ﴿وَلاَ يَحِيقُ المَكْرُ السَّيِّءُ إلاَّ بِأَهْلِهِ﴾.

nahhas-meani:12-12.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُل لِّمَن مَّا فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ؟ قُل للَّهِ﴾.
This is an argument against them, because they acknowledged that what is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah; so Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ to argue against them that the One who created what is in the heavens and the earth is able to bring them back to life after death.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كَتَبَ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ﴾.
Because He granted them respite until the Day of Resurrection.
It is possible that this is the end of the statement.
It is also possible that this (ما) is an explanation, because His saying ﴿لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ إِلَىٰ يَوْمِ ٱلْقِيَامَةِ لاَ رَيْبَ فِيهِ﴾ means "He grants you respite", and this is part of His mercy, Majestic and Mighty is He. [Translator's note: so in the source, «(ما) هذه»; there is no ما in the passage, and the reference is presumably to the following clause (لَيَجْمَعَنَّكُمْ) as an explanation of الرحمة.]

nahhas-meani:13-13.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿وَلَهُ مَا سَكَنَ فِي ٱلْلَّيْلِ وَٱلنَّهَارِ﴾.
That is: what is settled (in them); and this too is an argument against them.

nahhas-meani:14-14.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَهُوَ يُطْعِمُ وَلاَ يُطْعَمُ﴾.
Just as you say: He provides and is not provided for; He sustains and is not sustained.
It is related from al-Aʿmash that he read: وهو "يُطعِمُ ولا يَطْعَم", and it is a good reading, i.e. "and He does not eat."

nahhas-meani:16-16.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مَّن يُصْرَفْ عَنْهُ يَوْمَئِذٍ فَقَدْ رَحِمَهُ﴾.
The meaning is: whoever He turns the punishment away from; then (the object) was omitted because the hearer knows it; and likewise is the meaning of "مَنْ يُصْرَفْ" (the passive reading). [Translator's note: the first form is presumably the active reading «مَن يَصْرِفْ», though the source vocalises the verse as passive.]

nahhas-meani:19-19.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ هَـٰذَا ٱلْقُرْآنُ لأُنذِرَكُمْ بِهِ وَمَن بَلَغَ﴾.
The meaning is: and whomever the Qurʾān reaches (بَلَغَهُ); then the hāʾ (the object pronoun) was omitted because of the length of the noun (i.e. the relative noun with its ṣila).
Mujāhid said: And whoever embraces Islam, Arab or non-Arab.
It is related that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Convey the Qurʾān from Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He; whoever a verse of the Book of Allah reaches, the command of Allah has reached him."
It has also been said: the meaning is "and whoever reaches puberty", as one says: "So-and-so has reached (i.e. come of age)."

nahhas-meani:20-20.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ آتَيْنَاهُمُ ٱلْكِتَابَ يَعْرِفُونَهُ كَمَا يَعْرِفُونَ أَبْنَآءَهُمُ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning (of the pronoun) is the Qurʾān.
But the ḥadīth indicates that the meaning is: they recognise the Prophet ﷺ.
It is related that ʿUmar said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām: "Do you recognise Muḥammad ﷺ as you recognise your son?" He said: "Yes, and more. Allah sent His trustee in His heaven to His trustee on His earth with his description, so I recognised him; whereas my son — I do not know what might have happened on his mother's part."

nahhas-meani:23-23.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ثُمَّ لَمْ تَكُنْ فِتْنَتُهُمْ إِلاَّ أَن قَالُواْ وَٱللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: The interpretation of this verse is very subtle. Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, told the stories of the idolaters and their infatuation (iftitān) with their idolatry; then He told that their infatuation, when they saw the realities, amounted to nothing but their disowning idolatry. The parallel to this in the language is that you see a man who loves someone who is misguided, and when that one falls into ruin he disowns him, so one says to him: "Your love for him was nothing but your disowning him."
As for the meaning of their saying ﴿وَٱللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ﴾ while He said in another place ﴿وَلاَ يَكْتُمُونَ اللَّهَ حَدِيثَاً﴾: (the latter) is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it, and the meaning is: and they will wish that they had not concealed any statement from Allah. The proof of the soundness of this view is that:
It is related from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr regarding His saying ﴿وَٱللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ﴾ that he said: They made excuses and swore oaths; and likewise said Ibn Abī Najīḥ and Qatāda.
It is related from Mujāhid that he said: When they saw sins being forgiven except idolatry, and people coming out of the Fire except the idolaters, they said: ﴿وَٱللَّهِ رَبِّنَا مَا كُنَّا مُشْرِكِينَ﴾.
As for the statement of some philologists that they only said this believing themselves truthful, and that they would not lie having witnessed what they witnessed — and Quṭrub holds this view — it is a rejected view, because he said "they would not lie", whereas after it comes ﴿انْظُرْ كَيْفَ كَذَبُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾. What makes the error in this view clear to you is His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يَوْمَ يَبْعَثُهُمُ اللَّهُ جَمِيعَاً فَيَحْلِفُونَ لَهُ﴾ (to the end of) the verse.
Mujāhid said: Allah declared them liars.
It has also been said: the meaning of ﴿وَلاَ يَكْتُمُونَ اللَّهَ حَدِيثَاً﴾ is that it is manifest to Him.

nahhas-meani:25-25.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمِنْهُمْ مَّن يَسْتَمِعُ إِلَيْكَ، وَجَعَلْنَا عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ أَكِنَّةً أَن يَفْقَهُوهُ وَفِيۤ آذَانِهِمْ وَقْراً﴾.
It has been said: this was done to them as a requital for their disbelief. The meaning is not that they do not hear and do not understand; rather, since they did not benefit from what they heard and did not submit to the truth, they were in the position of one who does not hear and does not understand.
Then He told of their obstinacy, saying: ﴿وَإِن يَرَوْاْ كُلَّ آيَةٍ لاَّ يُؤْمِنُواْ بِهَا﴾, because when they saw the moon split they said "Sorcery!" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, told of their rejecting the signs without any argument, and said: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءُوكَ يُجَادِلُونَكَ يَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوۤاْ إِنْ هَـٰذَآ إِلاَّ أَسَاطِيرُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾, thereby telling that this is the extent of their argument.

nahhas-meani:26-26.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَهُمْ يَنْهَوْنَ عَنْهُ وَيَنْأَوْنَ عَنْهُ﴾.
Most of the exegetes hold that the meaning refers to the disbelievers, i.e. they forbid (others) from following the Prophet ﷺ and keep away from him.
Mujāhid said: He means by it Quraysh.
Likewise Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: He means by it the disbelievers.
Sufyān related from Ḥabīb ibn Abī Thābit, who said: Someone who heard Ibn ʿAbbās informed me that he said: It was revealed about "Abū Ṭālib"; he used to forbid (people) from harming the Prophet ﷺ, yet kept himself distant from him.
The first view is more fitting, because it is connected with the reports about the disbelievers and their statements.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِن يُهْلِكُونَ إِلاَّ أَنفُسَهُمْ﴾.
That is: the evil consequence of that returns upon them, because Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, scatters their gatherings [and gives him victory over them].
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَا يَشْعُرُونَ﴾.
That is: and they do not perceive that the evil consequence of that returns upon them.

nahhas-meani:27-27.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَىٰ إِذْ وُقِفُواْ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ﴾.
On its meaning there are three views:
1 - Among them, that the meaning of ﴿وُقِفُواْ عَلَى ٱلنَّارِ﴾ is "they were made to enter it", as one says وقفتُ على ما عند فلان, i.e. I came to know its reality.
2 - It has also been said: its meaning is "they saw it".
3 - And it has been said: they passed over it while it was beneath them.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَقَالُواْ يٰلَيْتَنَا نُرَدُّ وَلاَ نُكَذِّبُ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّنَا وَنَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾.
The meaning is: and we do not deny the signs of our Lord, whether we are sent back or not.
Sībawayh said: Similar to it is دعني ولا أعود ("Leave me, and I will not do it again"), i.e. I will not do it again whether you leave me or not.
Whoever reads ﴿وَلاَ نُكَذِّبَ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّنَا وَنَكُونَ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ (in the accusative), its meaning for him is: would that the sending back happened to us, and that we would not deny.
Abū Isḥāq said: It contains the meaning: if we are sent back, we will not deny.
Ibn ʿĀmir read ﴿يا لَيْتَنَا نُرَدُّ وَلاَ نُكَذِّبَ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّنَا وَنَكُونَ مِنَ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ with the accusative. [Translator's note: so in the source; Ibn ʿĀmir's reading is usually reported as نُكَذِّبُ in the nominative and نَكُونَ in the accusative, whereas the text as written here shows both verbs in the accusative.]
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read: ﴿ولا نُكَذِّبُ بِآيَاتِ رَبِّنَا وَنَكُونُ مِنَ المؤمنين﴾.
Ubayy ibn Kaʿb read: ﴿ولا نكذِّبُ بآيَاتِ رَبِّنَا أبَداً﴾.

nahhas-meani:28-28.t:
And He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿بَلْ بَدَا لَهُمْ مَّا كَانُواْ يُخْفُونَ مِن قَبْلُ﴾.
The meaning is: rather, there became manifest to those who followed the misleaders what the misleaders used to hide from them concerning the resurrection and the Day of Resurrection, because after it comes: ﴿وَقَالُوا إِنْ هِيَ إِلاَّ حَيَاتُنَا الدُّنْيَا وَمَا نَحْنُ بِمَبْعُوثِينَ﴾.
Some philologists said: (In) "and if they were sent back they would return to what they were forbidden" there is something omitted, and the meaning is: if they were sent back before they witnessed the punishment, because they would not disbelieve after having witnessed (it).
This view is rejected, because Allah, Majestic is His praise, has told of them that they will say this on the Day of Resurrection; and He, Majestic and Mighty is He, has told of Iblīs that he disbelieved after he had seen, and of them that they disbelieved out of obstinacy and preference for leadership.

nahhas-meani:31-31.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿جَآءَتْهُمُ ٱلسَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً﴾.
البغتة is suddenness.
One says: بَغَتَهم الأمرُ يَبْغَتُهم بَغْتاً وبَغْتَةً (the matter came upon them suddenly).
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالُواْ يٰحَسْرَتَنَا عَلَىٰ مَا فَرَّطْنَا فِيهَا﴾.
The point of addressing regret (ḥasra) in the vocative (nidāʾ), and things like it which do not answer, is that the Arabs, when they want to magnify something and draw attention to it, address it in the vocative; and from this is their saying: يَا عَجَبَاه (O wonder!).
Sībawayh said: When you say يا عَجَبَاه its meaning is "Be present and come, O wonder, for this is your time"; and this is more eloquent than your saying "I wondered." And from this is the poet's saying:
* فيا عَجَبَاً مِنْ رَحْلِها المُتَحَمِّلِ * (O what a wonder at her saddle being carried off!)
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَهُمْ يَحْمِلُونَ أَوْزَارَهُمْ عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِمْ﴾.
The singular of الأوزار is وِزْرٌ, and the verb from it is وَزَرَ يَزِرُ; what is meant by it is sin, and it is a figurative image. Its origin is الوَزَرُ, which is the mountain (i.e. a refuge).
From it is the ḥadīth about the women who went out with a funeral procession, and he said to them: "Go back burdened with sin (مَوْزوراتٍ), not rewarded."
Abū ʿUbayd said: The common people say "مأزوراتٍ" — as if, in his view, it had no justification, because it is from الوزر. And from it one says وزيرٌ (minister), as though he bears the burden for his master.

nahhas-meani:33-33.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ لاَ يُكْذِبُونَكَ﴾.
Thus it is related that ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, read it, and it is the choice of Abū ʿUbayd. He argued that it is related that Abū Jahl said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We do not call you a liar (لا نُكْذِبُكَ), but we deny what you have brought", so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ لاَ يُكَذِّبُونَكَ﴾. [Translator's note: so in the source; for Abū ʿUbayd's argument one would expect the verse here to be cited with the light form, يُكْذِبُونَكَ.]
Abū ʿUbayd was opposed in this: it was related (as) "لا نُكَذِّبُكَ", so Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, revealed ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ لاَ يُكَذِّبُونَكَ﴾. What strengthens this is that it is related that a man recited to Ibn ʿAbbās ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ لاَ يكْذِبُونَكَ﴾, and Ibn ʿAbbās said to him: ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ لاَ يُكَذِّبُونَكَ﴾, because they used to call the Prophet ﷺ "al-Amīn" (the Trustworthy).
The meaning of (يُكْذِبُونَكَ), according to the philologists, is: they attribute lying to you and report against you what you said. [Translator's note: so in the source; the explanations of the two forms appear to be reversed relative to the following sentence and to al-Kisāʾī's report at the end of the entry.]
The meaning of (لا يُكَذِّبُونَكَ) is: they do not find you a liar, just as you say أَحْمَدْتُه when you have found him praiseworthy.
It is also possible that the meaning of the light form is: they do not demonstrate against you that you are a liar, because one says أكذبتُه when you have argued against him and shown that he is a liar.
Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar al-Anbārī narrated to us: Shuʿayb ibn Ayyūb al-Wāsiṭī narrated to us, from Muʿāwiya ibn Hishām, from Sufyān al-Thawrī, from Abū Isḥāq, from Nājiya ibn Kaʿb, from ʿAlī, who said: Abū Jahl said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We do not call you a liar (لا نُكْذِبُكَ), but we deny what you have brought." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿فَإِنَّهُمْ لاَ يُكَذِّبُونَكَ، وَلَـٰكِنَّ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ بِآيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ يَجْحَدُونَ﴾.
The (correct) view in this is the position of Abū ʿUbayd, and his argument is binding, because ʿAlī, Allah's mercy be upon him, is the one who related the ḥadīth, and it is authentically reported from him that he read it with the light form (takhfīf).
Al-Kisāʾī reported from the Arabs: أكذبتُ الرّجلَ: I reported that he brought a lie and related it; and كذَّبتُه: I reported that he is a liar.

nahhas-meani:35-35.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَإِن ٱسْتَطَعْتَ أَن تَبْتَغِيَ نَفَقاً فِي ٱلأَرْضِ أَوْ سُلَّماً فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾.
Qatāda said: النّفقُ is a passage (الشِّرْب) in the earth, and السُّلَّمُ is steps. [Translator's note: «الشِّرْب» is so in the source; the word is perhaps a corruption of «السَّرَب» (tunnel).]
So it is in the language too; and from it is النافقاء: one of the burrow-holes of the jerboa.
Abū Isḥāq said: السُّلَّمُ is derived from السَّلاَمة (safety), as though it delivers you safely to the place you want.
The meaning is: if you are able to seek a tunnel in the earth or a ladder into the sky and bring them a sign, then do so. Then this (apodosis) was omitted because the hearer knows it, i.e. the matter is not in your hands at all.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ لَجَمَعَهُمْ عَلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰ﴾.
That is: He would have shown them a sign compelling them to believe; but He, Majestic and Mighty is He, willed to reward whoever of them believed and whoever did good.
It is also possible that the meaning is: He would have stamped them with faith.

nahhas-meani:36-36.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّمَا يَسْتَجِيبُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسْمَعُونَ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid said: The believers are meant by it, and the meaning is: those who hear with the hearing of acceptance.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱلْمَوْتَىٰ يَبْعَثُهُمُ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
Al-Ḥasan and Mujāhid said: The disbelievers are meant by it.
Others said: Every dead person is meant by it.

nahhas-meani:38-38.t:
And His saying, Majestic is His majesty: ﴿وَمَا مِن دَآبَّةٍ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ، وَلاَ طَائِرٍ يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ، إِلاَّ أُمَمٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ﴾.
Most of the exegetes hold that the meaning is: they are created as you are created, and are resurrected as you are resurrected.
Likewise Abū Hurayra said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, will gather on the Day of Resurrection the birds and the beasts, and such will be His justice that He will take (retribution) from the horned one for the hornless one; then He will say: "Become dust!" At that the disbeliever will say: ﴿يَا لَيْتَنِي كُنْتُ تُرَابَاً﴾.
Mujāhid said about His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He, ﴿إِلاَّ أُمَمٌ أَمْثَالُكُمْ﴾: (They are) kinds, having names by which they are known, as you are known.
The meaning of ﴿يَطِيرُ بِجَنَاحَيْهِ﴾ is by way of tawkīd (emphasis), because you may say "I flew (i.e. hastened) about my business."

nahhas-meani:40-40.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُكُم إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُ ٱللَّهِ أَوْ أَتَتْكُمْ ٱلسَّاعَةُ﴾.
The meaning is: or the Hour in which you will be resurrected comes to you.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ تَدْعُونَ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾.
In this is the greatest argument against them, because they used to worship idols, yet when they fell into hardship they called upon Allah.

nahhas-meani:136-136.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ مِمَّا ذَرَأَ مِنَ ٱلْحَرْثِ وَٱلأَنْعَامِ نَصِيباً﴾.
There is an ellipsis (ḥadhf) in the passage; the meaning is: and they assigned a share to their idols, and this is indicated by ﴿فَقَالُواْ هَـٰذَا لِلَّهِ بِزَعْمِهِمْ وَهَـٰذَا لِشُرَكَآئِنَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: They used to assign one portion to Allah and one portion to their partners; if what belonged to their partners was lost, they compensated for it from what belonged to Allah, but if what belonged to Allah was lost, they compensated nothing for it.
He said: The livestock (al-anʿām) means the baḥīra and the sāʾiba.
Qatāda said: They used to assign a share to Allah and a share to their partners; if a camel from what belonged to their partners perished, they took from what belonged to Allah and gave it to their partners, but if a camel from what belonged to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, perished, they left it and said: Allah has no need of this. And when a year of drought struck them, they took what belonged to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, slaughtered it and ate it.
And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿سَآءَ مَا يَحْكُمُونَ﴾.
So Allah censured that deed of theirs.
And it is said: ذرَأ، يَذْرَأُ، ذَرْءً, meaning: he created.

nahhas-meani:137-137.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ زَيَّنَ لِكَثِيرٍ مِّنَ ٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ قَتْلَ أَوْلاَدِهِمْ شُرَكَآؤُهُمْ﴾.
It means: the girl buried alive (al-mawʾūda).
Mujāhid said: The devils made the killing of daughters seem fair to them, and made them fear poverty.
Someone other than Mujāhid said: "شركاؤُهُمْ" here means those who serve the idols.

nahhas-meani:138-138.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقَالُواْ هَـٰذِهِ أَنْعَامٌ وَحَرْثٌ حِجْرٌ﴾.
Qatāda said: الحِجْرُ means the forbidden.
And it is said: These were things they used to assign to their idols, and none ate of them except whomever the servants of the idols wished.
And the tillage (al-ḥarth) is what they used to assign for the expenses of their idols, and they forbade it to people except its servants.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَنْعَامٌ حُرِّمَتْ ظُهُورُهَا﴾.
Qatāda said: He means the sāʾiba and the waṣīla.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَنْعَامٌ لاَّ يَذْكُرُونَ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا﴾.
That is, they slaughter them for their gods and do not mention the name of Allah over them. So Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, made known that He had not commanded them to do this, nor had a prophet brought it to them [Translator's note: the text reads «بن نبيٌّ», apparently a misprint for «به نبيٌّ», "nor had a prophet brought it to them"], and so He the Exalted said: ﴿ٱفْتِرَآءً عَلَيْهِ سَيَجْزِيهِم بِمَا كَانُواْ يَفْتَرُونَ﴾.
And it is said: the meaning of ﴿وَأَنْعَامٌ حُرِّمَتْ ظُهُورُهَا﴾
is the ḥāmī which Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, mentioned in His saying: ﴿وَلاَ وَصِيَلةٍ وَلاَ حَامٍ﴾.
And it is said: the meaning of ﴿وَأَنْعَامٌ لاَّ يَذْكُرُونَ ٱسْمَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا﴾ is the sāʾiba, because it is not ridden, such that the name of Allah would be mentioned over it.
And it is said: they slaughter them for their idols and do not mention the name of Allah over them.
And those whose backs are forbidden are "the sāʾiba, the ḥāmī and the baḥīra", and the soundest of these is what we began with.

nahhas-meani:139-139.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَقَالُواْ مَا فِي بُطُونِ هَـٰذِهِ ٱلأَنْعَامِ خَالِصَةٌ لِّذُكُورِنَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the baḥīra and the sāʾiba.
Someone else said: When they assigned to their idols something of what was in the bellies of the livestock, and it gave birth to a living male offspring, it belonged to the males to the exclusion of the females; and if it gave birth to a dead male, the males and females shared in it. Hence His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَإِن يَكُن مَّيْتَةً فَهُمْ فِيهِ شُرَكَآءُ﴾.
Quṭrub said: When she had borne twins ten times, whatever she bore after that belonged to the males, unless it died, in which case male and female shared in eating it.
Al-Aʿmash read: (وَقَالُوا مَا فِي بُطُونِ هَذِهِ الأَنْعَامِ خَالِصٌ لِذُكُورِنَا).
Al-Kisāʾī said: The meaning of خالصٌ and خالصةٌ is one, except that the hāʾ (the feminine ending) is for intensiveness (mubālagha), as one says: رجلٌ داهيةٌ (a very cunning man) and علاَّمةٌ (a very learned man).
And al-Farrāʾ said: The khāʾ [Translator's note: the text reads «الخاء»; evidently a misprint for «الهاء», the hāʾ, i.e. the feminine ending] is for the feminine gender of the livestock, because what is in the bellies of the livestock is like them.
And it was read: ﴿خَالِصُهُ لِذُكُورِنَا﴾.
And the meaning according to this reading is: whatever of it comes out alive is for our males.
﴿وَمُحَرَّمٌ عَلَىٰ أَزْوَاجِنَا﴾, that is, the females.
Mujāhid said: The meaning of ﴿سَيَجْزِيهِمْ وَصْفَهُمْ﴾ is: He will requite them for their lie.
And the implied construction (taqdīr) according to the grammarians is: He will requite them with the requital of their description, which is a lie.

nahhas-meani:140-140.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَدْ خَسِرَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَتَلُوۤاْ أَوْلاَدَهُمْ سَفَهاً بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾.
It means: their killing of daughters out of ignorance.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَحَرَّمُواْ مَا رَزَقَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱفْتِرَآءً عَلَى ٱللَّهِ قَدْ ضَلُّواْ وَمَا كَانُواْ مُهْتَدِينَ﴾.
Abū Razīn said: And they were not rightly guided before that either.

nahhas-meani:141-141.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنشَأَ جَنَّاتٍ مَّعْرُوشَاتٍ وَغَيْرَ مَعْرُوشَاتٍ﴾.
أنشَأَ: He created and originated. And الجنَّاتُ: the orchards.
And it is said: المعروشاتُ are the grapevines.
﴿وَٱلنَّخْلَ وَٱلزَّرْعَ مُخْتَلِفاً أُكُلُهُ﴾, that is, its fruit, because it is something that is eaten.
﴿وَٱلزَّيْتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ مُتَشَابِهاً وَغَيْرَ مُتَشَابِهٍ﴾.
It is said: alike in appearance and different in taste; among it is the sweet and the sour.
And it is said: some of it resembles other parts in taste, and some of it does not resemble other parts in taste.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كُلُواْ مِن ثَمَرِهِ إِذَآ أَثْمَرَ وَآتُواْ حَقَّهُ يَوْمَ حَصَادِهِ، وَلاَ تُسْرِفُوۤاْ إِنَّهُ لاَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُسْرِفِينَ﴾.
There are three views on this verse:
The position of Ibn ʿUmar, Abū al-Dardāʾ, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Abū al-ʿĀliya, Mujāhid and ʿAṭāʾ is that one must give charity from it apart from the obligatory zakāt.
The second view: that the verse is abrogated.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: It was abrogated by the tenth and the half-tenth.
And two views are reported from al-Ḥasan:
Sufyān reported from Yūnus from al-Ḥasan, who said: It was abrogated by the obligatory zakāt.
And the other view — which is the third view on the verse — was reported by Shuʿba from Abū al-Rajāʾ, who said: I asked al-Ḥasan about His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَآتُواْ حَقَّهُ يَوْمَ حَصَادِهِ﴾, and he said: The obligatory zakāt.
And likewise said Ibn ʿAbbās, Anas ibn Mālik, Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya, Jābir ibn Zayd, Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab, Ṭāwūs, Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
And Ibn Wahb reported it from Mālik, who said: It is the obligatory charity.
And the first view is the most fitting of them, because it is unlikely that the obligatory zakāt is meant by it, since al-Anʿām is Meccan, and zakāt was only made obligatory after the arrival of the Prophet ﷺ in Medina.
And what strengthens the first view is the ḥadīth of the Prophet ﷺ that he forbade harvesting dates at night.
Sufyān said: So that the poor may be present.
Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab said: And the meaning of ﴿وَلاَ تُسْرِفُوۤاْ﴾ is: do not refrain from charity and so perish.
And someone else said: The meaning of ﴿وَلاَ تُسْرِفُوۤاْ﴾ is: do not hand over all your wealth to strangers and leave your dependants, as it is narrated: "Begin with those you support."
السَّرَفُ in the language means going beyond into what is not permitted, and it is a term of censure; that is, do not spend in forbidden ways, such that the beggar finds nothing.
And it is said: The meaning of ﴿وَلاَ تُسْرِفُوۤاْ﴾ is: do not spend your wealth on what is not permitted, because He has reported of them that they said: ﴿وَهَذَا لِشُرَكَائِنَا﴾.

nahhas-meani:142-142.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلأَنْعَامِ حَمُولَةً وَفَرْشاً﴾.
Abū al-Aḥwaṣ reported from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he said: "الحَمُولةُ" is whatever of the camels is able to bear loads, and الفَرْشُ is whatever is not able to bear loads and is small.
Abū Jaʿfar said: And this is what is well known among most of the lexicographers.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: الحَمْولةُ is from the camels and the cattle, and الفرشُ is the sheep and goats.
And the proponent of this view adduced as evidence His saying ﴿ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾; he said: so ثمانية is a badal (substitute) for His saying ﴿حَمُولَةً وَفَرْشاً﴾.
Al-Ḥasan said: الحمولةُ is the camels, and الفَرْشُ is the sheep and goats.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كُلُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقَكُمُ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
It is a command signifying permission.
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿وَلاَ تَتَّبِعُواْ خُطُوَاتِ ٱلشَّيْطَانِ﴾.
It means: his ways, that is, his way which he makes seem good to you.
And it is said: his stepping over from the lawful to the unlawful.
And it is said: it means his traces.

nahhas-meani:143-143.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ثَمَانِيَةَ أَزْوَاجٍ﴾.
Every single thing that needs another is called by the Arabs زَوْجٌ (a mate, one of a pair).
* Then He the Exalted said: ﴿مَّنَ ٱلضَّأْنِ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾.
It is the plural of ضائن, as one says: راكب and رَكْبٌ.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلْمَعْزِ ٱثْنَيْنِ﴾.
This is an argument against them; that is: if He forbade the males, then every male is forbidden, and if He forbade the females, then every female is forbidden. He argued against them with this because they made lawful what was born alive — if male — for the males, and forbade it to the females if it was female.
Qatāda said: Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, commanded him to say to them: ﴿قُلْ ءَآلذَّكَرَيْنِ حَرَّمَ أَمِ ٱلأُنثَيَيْنِ أَمَّا ٱشْتَمَلَتْ عَلَيْهِ أَرْحَامُ ٱلأُنثَيَيْنِ﴾ — if what the wombs of the two females contain is forbidden, then every offspring of them is forbidden, and all of them are offspring, so all of them are then forbidden; and if the prohibition is on account of the males of the sheep and goats, then every male is forbidden to you; and if it is on account of the females, then every female is forbidden to you. And they used to forbid the waṣīla and her brother to men and women.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿نَبِّئُونِي بِعِلْمٍ إِن كُنتُمْ صَادِقِينَ﴾.
That is, you have no knowledge, because they did not believe in a scripture.

nahhas-meani:144-144.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَمْ كُنتُمْ شُهَدَآءَ إِذْ وَصَّاكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِهَـٰذَا﴾.
That is, you do not believe in a scripture, so did you witness Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, forbidding this?
Then He made their wrongdoing clear, saying: ﴿فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً﴾? [verse 144].

nahhas-meani:145-145.t:
Then He made clear that Allah forbids nothing except by revelation, saying: ﴿قُل لاَّ أَجِدُ فِي مَآ أُوْحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّماً عَلَىٰ طَاعِمٍ يَطْعَمُهُ﴾.
It is reported from ʿĀʾisha — Allah's mercy be upon her — (عَلَى طَاعِمٍ طَعِمَهُ).
And from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī: ﴿طَاعِمٍ يَطَّعِمُهُ﴾.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَكُونَ مَيْتَةً أَوْ دَماً مَّسْفُوحاً﴾.
Qatāda said: المسفوحُ means poured out; so He forbade specifically what was poured out, whereas what is mixed with the meat is lawful.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَإِنَّهُ رِجْسٌ، أَوْ فِسْقاً أُهِلَّ لِغَيْرِ ٱللَّهِ بِهِ﴾.
That is, slaughtered for other than Allah, with a name other than the name of Allah mentioned over it. He called it "فِسْقاً" (transgression) because it departs from the religion.
And the meaning is: or blood poured out, or the flesh of swine, or a transgression consecrated to other than Allah — for it is filth.
And the beast killed by a blow (al-mawqūdha), the one killed by a fall (al-mutaraddiya) and the one gored to death (al-naṭīḥa) are included in this verse according to some, because they are kinds of carrion.
As for what is not included in this verse according to some, there are two views on it:
One of them: that it is reported from ʿĀʾisha and Ibn ʿAbbās that the verse comprehends everything forbidden among animals specifically, and that among animals nothing is forbidden except what is mentioned in it.
And the other view: that this verse is muḥkam (unabrogated, of decisive meaning), comprehending animals and other things.
And there are other things that Allah has forbidden besides these; it is authentically established from the Prophet ﷺ that he (forbade the flesh of domestic donkeys, every fanged beast of prey, and every bird with talons).
And it was said: This is a strong view linguistically, because "ما" is vague (mubham), so His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُل لاَّ أَجِدُ فِي مَآ أُوْحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّماً﴾ must be general, covering animals and other things. And Allah knows best what He intended.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَمَنِ ٱضْطُرَّ غَيْرَ بَاغٍ وَلاَ عَادٍ﴾.
The best of what has been said about the bāghī: the one who eats out of compulsion, not for pleasure.
And the ʿādī: the one who goes beyond what keeps him alive.

nahhas-meani:146-146.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ حَرَّمْنَا كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ﴾.
Mujāhid, Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿كُلَّ ذِي ظُفُرٍ﴾ is the camels and the ostriches.
Qatāda said: And among birds it is whatever is not cloven-clawed, such as the duck and what resembles it. And according to the lexicographers it is, among birds, whatever has talons, and included in it is whatever of the birds hunts with its claw, and all kinds of beasts of prey, dogs and cats.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلْبَقَرِ وَٱلْغَنَمِ حَرَّمْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ شُحُومَهُمَآ إِلاَّ مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَا﴾.
Qatāda said: It is specifically the fat of the omenta (al-thurūb).
And the position of Ibn Jurayj: that it is every fat that is not mixed with bone nor lies on bone.
And this is more fitting because of the generality of the verse, and because of the ḥadīth with a connected chain (musnad): "May Allah fight the Jews! Fats were forbidden to them, so they melted them down, sold them and consumed their price."
﴿إِلاَّ مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَا﴾, that is, except the fat of the flanks and what clings to the back, for these were not forbidden to them.
﴿أَوِ ٱلْحَوَايَآ﴾.
Mujāhid and Qatāda said: الحوايا are the intestines where dung collects (al-mabāʿir).
Abū ʿUbayda said: In my view it is whatever of the belly is coiled, that is, curved round.
Al-Kisāʾī said: Its singular is حاوية and حوَّية.
And Sībawayh related: حاوياء. It is said: The meaning is: We forbade them their fats; then He made an exception, saying: ﴿إِلاَّ مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَا﴾, then He conjoined to the excepted, saying: ﴿أَوِ ٱلْحَوَايَآ أَوْ مَا ٱخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ﴾, that is, except these things, for they are lawful.
And it is said: The meaning is: We forbade them their fats, or the entrails, or what is mixed with bone, except what their backs carry. So what comes after (إلاَّ) on this view is an exception, [the rest] being included in the prohibition, and it is like His saying the Exalted: ﴿وَلاَ تُطِعْ مِنْهُمْ آثِمَاً أَوْ كَفُورَاً﴾, and (أو) here is not in the sense of the wāw, that is: do not obey this sort.
And al-Kisāʾī said: ﴿إِلاَّ مَا حَمَلَتْ ظُهُورُهُمَا﴾ — (ما) is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) by exception, and الحوايا is in the position of the nominative (rafʿ), in the sense of: and what the entrails carry; so he conjoined الحوايا to الظهور.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَوْ مَا ٱخْتَلَطَ بِعَظْمٍ﴾.
He said: so He conjoined it to the excepted. This is one of the two views of al-Farrāʾ, and it is the soundest of these views. And Allah knows best.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ذٰلِكَ جَزَيْنَاهُم بِبَغْيِهِمْ وِإِنَّا لَصَادِقُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: These things were forbidden to them as a punishment for their transgression.

nahhas-meani:147-147.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَإِن كَذَّبُوكَ فَقُلْ رَّبُّكُمْ ذُو رَحْمَةٍ وَاسِعَةٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the Jews.

nahhas-meani:148-148.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿سَيَقُولُ ٱلَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُواْ لَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَآ أَشْرَكْنَا وَلاَ آبَاؤُنَا، وَلاَ حَرَّمْنَا مِن شَيْءٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the unbelievers of Quraysh, that is: Allah willed [Translator's note: the text reads «أي شاء الله»; the sense of the verse suggests «لو شاء الله», "had Allah willed"] we would not have forbidden the baḥīra or the sāʾiba.
And someone else said: So Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, rejected this statement of theirs and said: ﴿كَذٰلِكَ كَذَّبَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِم﴾, because they may not argue that whoever is engaged in disobedience which Allah willed to be has an excuse in that; for if it were so, then whoever opposed them in their religion would have an excuse too, because had Allah willed to guide him, He would have guided him.

nahhas-meani:149-149.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ فَلِلَّهِ ٱلْحُجَّةُ ٱلْبَالِغَةُ﴾.
That is, by His sending the messengers and His making the clear proofs manifest.

nahhas-meani:150-150.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ هَلُمَّ شُهَدَآءَكُمُ ٱلَّذِينَ يَشْهَدُونَ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ حَرَّمَ هَـٰذَا﴾.
The origin according to al-Khalīl: (هَا) to which (لُمَّ) was joined, then the alif was elided because of frequent use.
And someone else said: The origin is (هَلْ) to which (لُمَّ) was added.
And it is said: it keeps its form, in the sense of (هاتِ) "bring".
The people of the Ḥijāz say هلمَّ to one, two and a group alike, while the people of Najd add the marker [of number and gender] as is done with all other verbs.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَهُم بِرَبِّهِمْ يَعْدِلُونَ﴾.
That is, they set up an equal (ʿidl) to Him and so worship other than Him, Majestic and Mighty is He.

nahhas-meani:151-151.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُلْ تَعَالَوْاْ أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَلاَّ تُشْرِكُواْ بِهِ شَيْئاً﴾.
It is said: What he recited to them was: ﴿قُلْ لاَ أَجِدُ فِيمَا أُوحِيَ إِلَيَّ مُحَرَّماً عَلَى طَاعِمِ يَطْعَمُهُ﴾ to the end of the verse.
And the meaning of ﴿أَنْ تَقوُلُوا إِنَّمَا أُنْزِلَ الكِتَابُ عَلَى طَائِفَتَيْنِ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا﴾ [thus it is] would be: [lest] you say.
And some grammarians say the meaning is: so that you do not say (لئلاَّ تقولوا).
And according to the Basrans, the elision of (لا) is not permissible.
And it is said: The meaning is: He enjoined you not to associate partners.
And it is said: The meaning is: Say, come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you; [that is,] He made clear what He forbade, and said: that you associate nothing with Him.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَبِٱلْوَالِدَيْنِ إِحْسَاناً﴾.
That is: and do good to parents, an iḥsān (doing good) [as a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object)].
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The muḥkam (decisive) verses are ﴿قُلْ تَعَالَوْاْ أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ to the end of three verses.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْتُلُوۤاْ أَوْلاَدَكُمْ مِّنْ إِمْلاَقٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: الإِملاقُ means destitution.
And al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "When a daughter was born to one of them, he would bury her alive for fear of poverty."
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْرَبُواْ ٱلْفَوَاحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ﴾.
Qatāda said: He means their secret and their open forms. He said: They used to conceal fornication with a free woman and do it openly with a slave woman.
Mujāhid said: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْرَبُواْ مَالَ الْيَتِيمِ إِلاَّ بِالَّتِي هِيَ أَحْسَنُ﴾ — [this is] trading with it.
And do not buy anything from it, and do not borrow [from it].

nahhas-meani:153-153.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَنَّ هَـٰذَا صِرَاطِي مُسْتَقِيماً﴾.
Ibn Abī Isḥāq and Yaʿqūb read: ﴿وَأَنْ هَذَا صِرَاطِيَ مُسْتَقِيمَاً﴾ with the lightened form of (أنَّ). And it is also read (إِنَّ) with kasra on the hamza.
Whoever reads (وَأَنَّ هَذَا), it is in his view in the sense of: and recite to them that this….
And it is possible that the meaning is: and He enjoined you that this….
And whoever reads with the lightened (أَنْ), its meaning may be according to this, and it is possible that (أنْ) is redundant (zāʾida) for emphasis, as He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَنْ جَاءَ البَشِيرُ﴾.
And whoever reads (وإنَّ هذا) cuts it off from what precedes it [as a new sentence].
And it is reported from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd — may Allah have mercy on him — that he drew a line on the ground and said: Thus is the straight path, and the paths are around it, and with every path is a devil.
Mujāhid said: The paths (al-subul) are innovations and doubtful matters.

nahhas-meani:154-154.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ثُمَّ آتَيْنَا مُوسَى ٱلْكِتَابَ تَمَاماً عَلَى ٱلَّذِيۤ أَحْسَنَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The meaning is: upon the believer who does good.
And al-Ḥasan said: Among them were some who did good and some who did not, and the Book was sent down as a completion upon the one who did good.
And the proof of the soundness of this view is that Ibn Masʿūd read: ﴿تَمَامَاً عَلَى الَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا﴾.
And it is said: The meaning of ﴿تَمَاماً عَلَى ٱلَّذِيۤ أَحْسَنَ﴾ is: [upon what] Mūsā did well, of obedience to Allah and following His command.
Ibn Yaʿmar and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read ﴿عَلَى الَّذِي أَحْسَنُ﴾.
And the meaning is: upon that which is the best of things.
As for the meaning of (ثُمَّ), it indicates that the second comes after the first —
yet the story of Mūsā ﷺ and his being given the Book was before this?
The answer is that it is a report from Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, and the meaning is: Say, come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you; then recite what We gave Mūsā.

nahhas-meani:156-156.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَن تَقُولُوۤاْ إِنَّمَآ أُنزِلَ ٱلْكِتَابُ عَلَىٰ طَآئِفَتَيْنِ مِن قَبْلِنَا﴾.
The best of what has been said about this is: out of aversion that you should say.
Abū Jaʿfar said: We have already explained what has been said about it.
Qatāda said: By the two groups He means the Jews and the Christians.
And he said: By "the study" (al-dirāsa) He means recitation.

nahhas-meani:157-157.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَوْ تَقُولُواْ لَوْ أَنَّآ أُنزِلَ عَلَيْنَا ٱلْكِتَابُ لَكُنَّآ أَهْدَىٰ مِنْهُمْ﴾.
﴿أَهْدَىٰ مِنْهُمْ﴾: of better understanding than they, because they [the Arabs] memorised their poems and their reports, though they were unlettered.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّن كَذَّبَ بِآيَاتِ ٱللَّهِ وَصَدَفَ عَنْهَا﴾.
Qatāda said about His saying ﴿وَصَدَفَ عَنْهَا﴾: that is, he turned away.

nahhas-meani:158-158.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿هَلْ يَنظُرُونَ إِلاَّ أَن تَأْتِيهُمُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, with death.
﴿أَوْ يَأْتَ رَبُّكَ﴾ — Qatāda said: He means the Day of Resurrection.
And someone else said: The meaning is: your Lord's destroying them.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَ رَبُّكَ أَوْ يَأْتِيَ بَعْضُ آيَاتِ رَبِّكَ، يَوْمَ يَأْتِي بَعْضُ آيَاتِ رَبِّكَ لاَ يَنفَعُ نَفْساً إِيمَانُهَا لَمْ تَكُنْ آمَنَتْ مِن قَبْلُ، أَوْ كَسَبَتْ فِيۤ إِيمَانِهَا خَيْراً﴾.
Wakīʿ reported from Ibn Abī Laylā, from ʿAṭiyya, from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, ﴿يَوْمَ يَأْتِي بَعْضُ آيَاتِ رَبِّكَ﴾: he said: The rising of the sun from its place of setting.
﴿لم تكن آمنت من قبلُ أو كسبت في إيمانها خيراً﴾.
And Ibn Jurayj reported from Ibn Abī Mulayka from ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr, who said: "The sign at which its faith will not benefit a soul: when the sun rises from its place of setting together with the moon at one time."

nahhas-meani:159-159.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ فَرَّقُواْ دِينَهُمْ وَكَانُواْ شِيَعاً لَّسْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ﴾.
الشِّيَع means sects, and the meaning of شايعتُ in the language is: I followed.
And the meaning of ﴿وَكَانُواْ شِيَعاً﴾: and they were sects, each sect's members following one another, except that the shiyaʿ are all [internally] in agreement.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لَّسْتَ مِنْهُمْ فِي شَيْءٍ إِنَّمَآ أَمْرُهُمْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ﴾.
It is said: This was before the command to fight.
And Abū Ghālib reported from Abū Umāma, from the Prophet ﷺ, concerning His saying the Exalted ﴿فَرَّقُواْ دِينَهُمْ وَكَانُواْ شِيَعاً﴾: he said: They are the Khawārij.
And it is said: The verse indicates that whoever innovates, whether a Khārijī or another, the Prophet ﷺ has nothing to do with them, because when they innovate they dispute and split up, and become sects.

nahhas-meani:160-160.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿مَن جَآءَ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا، وَمَن جَآءَ بِٱلسَّيِّئَةِ فَلاَ يُجْزَىۤ إِلاَّ مِثْلَهَا﴾.
Al-Aʿmash reported from Abū Ṣāliḥ, who said: "The good deed is 'There is no god but Allah', and the evil deed is associating partners (shirk)."
And the meaning is: what was with Him is the utmost in requital; He gave ten times its like.

nahhas-meani:161-161.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّنِي هَدَانِي رَبِّيۤ إِلَىٰ صِرَاطٍ مُّسْتَقِيمٍ﴾.
الصِّراطُ is the road, and the meaning is: He made known to me the religion that is the truth.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿دِيناً قِيَماً مِّلَّةَ إِبْرَاهِيمَ حَنِيفاً﴾.
And القَيِّمُ means the straight; and whoever reads "قِيمَاً", it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) like الصِّغَرِ and الكِبَر.

nahhas-meani:162-162.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ إِنَّ صَلاَتِي وَنُسُكِي وَمَحْيَايَ وَمَمَاتِي للَّهِ رَبِّ ٱلْعَالَمِينَ﴾.
النُّسُكُ is the plural of النسيكة, which is the sacrificial animal; the origin of this is drawing near to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, and from it [one says: a man is] ناسكٌ (devout).
This was said only because they used to slaughter for other than Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He.

nahhas-meani:164-164.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ أَغَيْرَ ٱللَّهِ أَبْغِي رَبّاً، وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾? [verse 164].
The meaning of "أبغي" is: I want and I seek.

nahhas-meani:165-165.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَكُمْ خَلاَئِفَ ٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
He means the community of Muḥammad ﷺ.
And it is said: because they are the last of the communities, so they have succeeded those who were before them.
And it is said: because some of them succeed others, until the Hour comes upon them; and the ḥadīth strengthens this view.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَرَفَعَ بَعْضَكُمْ فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجَاتٍ لِّيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِي مَآ آتَاكُمْ﴾.
That is, He favoured some of you over others in provision.
﴿لِّيَبْلُوَكُمْ فِي مَآ آتَاكُمْ﴾, that is, to test you in what He gave you, and see how you give thanks; He already knew what would be, with a knowledge of the unseen, but requital falls only upon what is witnessed.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّ رَبَّكَ سَرِيعُ ٱلْعِقَابِ، وَإِنَّهُ لَغَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾.
For His punishment, Majestic and Mighty is He, even though most of it is on the Day of Resurrection — everything that is coming is near.
And it is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: Sūrat al-Anʿām was revealed in Mecca all at once, except three verses of it, which were revealed in Medina, namely His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ تَعَالَوْا أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ أَلاَّ تُشْرِكُوا بِهِ شَيْئِاً﴾ to the end of the verses.

nahhas-meani:41-41.t:
And He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿بَلْ إِيَّاهُ تَدْعُونَ فَيَكْشِفُ مَا تَدْعُونَ إِلَيْهِ إِنْ شَآءَ﴾.
This is majāz (figurative expression); the meaning is: and He removes the harm on account of which you called upon Him. It is like ﴿وَاسْألِ القَرْيَةَ﴾ in its figurative usage.

nahhas-meani:42-42.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَقَدْ أَرْسَلنَآ إِلَىٰ أُمَمٍ مِّن قَبْلِكَ فَأَخَذْنَاهُمْ بِٱلْبَأْسَآءِ وَٱلضَّرَّآءِ﴾.
It has been said: البأساءُ is hunger and poverty, and الضَرَّاءُ is loss of wealth, of lives through illness, and of crops.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَضَرَّعُونَ﴾.
That is: so that the servants might be in hope through humble supplication.

nahhas-meani:43-43.t:
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿فَلَوْلاۤ إِذْ جَآءَهُمْ بَأْسُنَا تَضَرَّعُواْ﴾.
That is: why then did they not (فهلاَّ)?
And Allah informed the Prophet that He had sent before him a messenger to a people whose hard-heartedness reached the point that they were seized with distress and adversity and yet did not humble themselves.

nahhas-meani:44-44.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا نَسُواْ مَا ذُكِّرُواْ بِهِ، فَتَحْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ أَبْوَابَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: (The gates) of the ease and comfort of this world.
The implied form (taqdīr) according to the philologists is: We opened to them the gates of everything that had been closed to them.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَإِذَا هُمْ مُّبْلِسُونَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: الملبسُ is the one who is grieving and remorseful. [Translator's note: «الملبس» is so in the source, for «المُبْلِس».]
Al-Farrāʾ said: المبلسُ is the one whose argument has been cut off.

nahhas-meani:45-45.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَقُطِعَ دَابِرُ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ﴾.
الدابر in the language is the last; one says دَبَرهم يدبرهم when he comes as the last of them.
In the ḥadīth from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: "Among people are those who come to the prayer only دَبَرِياً", i.e. at the end of its time.

nahhas-meani:46-46.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ سَمْعَكُمْ وَأَبْصَارَكُمْ وَخَتَمَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِكُمْ مَّنْ إِلَـٰهٌ غَيْرُ ٱللَّهِ يَأْتِيكُمْ بِهِ﴾.
The meaning is: what god other than Allah would bring you what was taken from you? The hāʾ (in بِهِ) is an allusion to the maṣdar (verbal noun), and therefore it is singular.
It is also possible that it refers back to السمع (hearing), like ﴿وَاللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ أَحَقُّ أَنْ يُرْضُوهُ﴾.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿ٱنْظُرْ كَيْفَ نُصَرِّفُ ٱلآيَاتِ ثُمَّ هُمْ يَصْدِفُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, they turn away from them.

nahhas-meani:47-47.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ إِنْ أَتَاكُمْ عَذَابُ ٱللَّهِ بَغْتَةً أَوْ جَهْرَةً﴾.
Mujāhid said: البغتةُ is that it comes upon them suddenly while they feel safe, and الجهرةُ is that it comes upon them while they are watching.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿هَلْ يُهْلَكُ إِلاَّ ٱلْقَوْمُ ٱلظَّالِمُونَ﴾.
That is: will any be destroyed but you? — because they disbelieved and were obstinate.

nahhas-meani:48-48.t:
And His saying, Majestic is His praise: ﴿وَمَا نُرْسِلُ ٱلْمُرْسَلِينَ إِلاَّ مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ﴾.
That is: We did not send them to bring the signs that were demanded; they only bring such signs as make their proofs manifest; their way is only to give good tidings and to warn.

nahhas-meani:50-50.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُل لاَّ أَقُولُ لَكُمْ عِندِي خَزَآئِنُ ٱللَّهِ وَلاۤ أَعْلَمُ ٱلْغَيْبَ﴾.
This is connected with His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لَوْلاَ نُزِّلَ عَلَيْهِ آيَةٌ مِنْ رَبِّهِ﴾, i.e. I do not say to you that I have the treasuries of Allah from which He provides and gives, nor do I know the unseen so as to tell you what is hidden from you, except through revelation; ﴿وَلاۤ أَقُولُ لَكُمْ إِنِّي مَلَكٌ﴾, because the angel witnesses of the affair of Allah, Majestic and Exalted is He, what human beings do not witness.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي ٱلأَعْمَىٰ وَٱلْبَصِيرُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the Muslim and the disbeliever.

nahhas-meani:51-51.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَنذِرْ بِهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ أَن يُحْشَرُوۤاْ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ﴾.
That is: with the Qurʾān. He singled out those who fear the gathering because the argument against them is more binding: if one is a Muslim, he is warned so that he abandons sins; and if he is of the People of the Book, he is warned so that he follows the truth.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لَيْسَ لَهُمْ مِّن دُونِهِ وَلِيٌّ وَلاَ شَفِيعٌ﴾.
Because the Jews and the Christians said: "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved ones."

nahhas-meani:52-52.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَطْرُدِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِٱلْغَدَاةِ وَٱلْعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ﴾.
Saʿd said: It was revealed about six: myself, ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd and four (others). The idolaters said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We are ashamed to be followers along with these", so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed: ﴿وَلاَ تَطْرُدِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ رَبَّهُمْ بِٱلْغَدَاةِ وَٱلْعَشِيِّ يُرِيدُونَ وَجْهَهُ﴾ up to His saying: ﴿أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بأَعْلَمَ بِالشَّاكِرِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: It was revealed about Bilāl and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd.
Someone else said: The idolaters only wanted by this to have an argument against the Prophet ﷺ, because the followers of the prophets are the poor; so they asked him to drive them away so that they could use it as an argument against him, and Allah protected him from what they wanted of him.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَا مِنْ حِسَابِكَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِّن شَيْءٍ فَتَطْرُدَهُمْ فَتَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾.
The meaning is: "And do not drive away those who call upon their Lord, lest you be among the wrongdoers; and nothing of your account is (upon them) that you should drive them away" — by way of advancing and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr).

nahhas-meani:53-53.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ فَتَنَّا بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ﴾.
That is: We tested and tried; because the poor bore hardship patiently despite their poverty, and that made the argument against the rich more binding.
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لِّيَقُولوۤاْ أَهَـٰؤُلاۤءِ مَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْهِم مِّن بَيْنِنَآ﴾.
That is: so that the rich would say.

nahhas-meani:54-54.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَقُلْ سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ﴾.
السَّلامُ and السَّلامةُ have one meaning; the meaning of "سلامٌ عليكم" is: may Allah keep you safe in your religion and your selves. And al-Salām is one of the names of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, its meaning being "the Possessor of safety".
Al-Ḥasan, ʿĀṣim and ʿĪsā read ﴿كَتَبَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ أَنَّهُ مَن عَمِلَ مِنكُمْ سُوۤءًا بِجَهَالَةٍ ثُمَّ تَابَ مِن بَعْدِهِ وَأَصْلَحَ فَأَنَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَّحِيمٌ﴾ with fatḥa on both (i.e. أَنَّهُ … فَأَنَّهُ). The first is a badal (substitute) for الرحمة, and the second is an emphatic repetition because of the length of the statement.
This is the position of Sībawayh.
Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, al-Aʿmash, Ibn Kathīr and Shibl read both with kasra (إِنَّهُ … فَإِنَّهُ).
The meaning in the first is "He said: indeed He…", and the second has kasra because it begins a new clause after the fāʾ.
The people of Medina read the first with fatḥa, because it is an explanation of الرحمة, and the second with kasra for the reason already given.

nahhas-meani:55-55.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ نفَصِّلُ ٱلآيَاتِ وَلِتَسْتَبِينَ سَبِيلَ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾.
The meaning on this reading (with سَبِيلَ in the accusative) is: and so that you, O Muḥammad, may discern the way of the criminals.
If it is said: but did he ﷺ not already discern it?
The answer according to al-Zajjāj is that the address to the Prophet ﷺ is an address to his community, so the meaning is: and so that you (all) may discern the way of the criminals.
If it is said: then why is the way of the believers not mentioned?
There are two answers to this:
One of them is that when the way of the criminals has been made clear, the way of the believers has (thereby) been made clear.
The other answer is that it is like His saying: ﴿سَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الحَرَّ﴾.
So the meaning is "and protect you from the cold", which was then omitted; and likewise here the meaning would be "and so that the way of the believers may become clear", which was then omitted.

nahhas-meani:57-57.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ إِنِّي عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍ مِّن رَّبِّي وَكَذَّبْتُم بِهِ مَا عِندِي مَا تَسْتَعْجِلُونَ بِهِ﴾.
That is: what you seek to hasten in demanding signs. It is also possible that the meaning is: the punishment you seek to hasten.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنِ ٱلْحُكْمُ إِلاَّ للَّهِ يَقُصُّ ٱلْحَقَّ﴾.
Thus read ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī and Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib. [Translator's note: so in the source; from the argument that follows, the reading attributed to these three is evidently يَقْضِ الحَقَّ ("He decides the truth"), while the text of the verse quoted here has يَقُصُّ.]
Some of those who read this reading argued that after it comes ﴿وَهُوَ خَيْرُ ٱلْفَاصِلِينَ﴾, and "judging (faṣl)" occurs only in deciding and ruling.
Ibn ʿAbbās, Mujāhid and al-Aʿraj read (يَقُصُّ الحَقَّ).
Ibn ʿAbbās said: (It is) as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ القَصَصِ﴾.
Some of those who read this reading argued that it is (written) in the codex text (al-sawād) without a yāʾ.
He said: And if it were يقضي, it would have been بالحقِّ (with the preposition).
This argument is not binding, because a yāʾ like this is frequently dropped (in writing).
As for his saying "if it were يقضي it would have been بالحق", that is not binding either, because the meaning of يقضي (can be) "he brings about and does", so the meaning is: He brings about the truth.
It is also possible that the meaning is: He decrees the true decree (i.e. الحقَّ is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar).

nahhas-meani:59-59.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَعِندَهُ مَفَاتِحُ ٱلْغَيْبِ لاَ يَعْلَمُهَآ إِلاَّ هُوَ﴾.
[The plural of مِفْتح is مفاتح, and the plural of مفتاح is مفاتيح.]
That is: the means of access to knowledge of the unseen.
Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan — known as Ibn Badīnā — narrated to us, he said: Abū Muṣʿab al-Zuhrī narrated to us, he said: Ṣāliḥ ibn Qudāma al-Jumaḥī narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, from Ibn ʿUmar, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The keys of the unseen are five, which none knows but Allah: none knows what the wombs fall short of but Allah; none knows what is in tomorrow but Allah; none knows when the rain will come but Allah; no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow; no soul knows in what land it will die; and none knows when the Hour will come but Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He." [Translator's note: the list as given contains six items.]
* And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَا تَسْقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلاَّ يَعْلَمُهَا﴾.
The meaning is that He knows it whether it falls or does not fall, just as you say "No one comes to you but that I know him" — it does not mean that you do not know him except while he is coming.
And (مِنْ) is for tawkīd (emphasis); the proof that it is for emphasis is that al-Ḥasan read ﴿وَلاَ رَطْبٌ وَلاَ يَابِسٌ إِلاَّ فِي كِتَابٍ مُبِينٍ﴾ (in the nominative, i.e. as if مِنْ were absent), that is, but that He knows it with certain knowledge.
It is also possible that the meaning is: but that He has written it before He created it.
And Allah knows best what He intended.
If it is asked: on this answer, what is the point of His writing it, when He knows it?
The answer to this is that it is to magnify the matter, i.e. know that this, in which there is neither reward nor punishment, is written down — so how much more what involves reward and punishment?

nahhas-meani:60-60.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَتَوَفَّاكُم بِٱللَّيْلِ﴾.
That is: He puts you to sleep, and takes the souls by which you discern, as Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿اللَّهُ يَتَوفَّى الأَنْفُسَ حَيِنَ مَوْتِهَا، وَالَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنَامِهَا﴾.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَيَعْلَمُ مَا جَرَحْتُم بِٱلنَّهَارِ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: That is, what you earned.
It is well known in the language that one says جرَح when he earns; and from it is ﴿وَمَا عَلَّمْتُمْ مِن الجَوَارِحِ مُكَلِّبِينَ﴾.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ثُمَّ يَبْعَثُكُمْ فِيهِ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said: That is, in the day.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لِيُقْضَىٰ أَجَلٌ مُّسَمًّى﴾.
That is: so that you may complete your term.

nahhas-meani:61-61.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿حَتَّىٰ إِذَا جَآءَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلْمَوْتُ تَوَفَّتْهُ رُسُلُنَا﴾.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: He means the helpers of the Angel of Death; they take the spirits and hand them over to the Angel of Death, or raise them up. So it is in the ḥadīth.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَهُمْ لاَ يُفَرِّطُونَ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: They do not slacken.
Someone else said: the meaning of فرَّطتُ is "I put forward incapacity".

nahhas-meani:63-63.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ مَن يُنَجِّيكُمْ مِّن ظُلُمَاتِ ٱلْبَرِّ وَٱلْبَحْرِ﴾.
الظلماتُ here are hardships. The Arabs say "a dark day" when it is severe, and when they make it out to be greater still they say "a day with stars (i.e. so dark the stars appear by day)". Sībawayh recited:
بَنِي أَسَدٍ لَوْ تَعْلَمونَ بَلاَءَنَا * إذَا كَانَ ذُو كَواكِبَ أَشْنَعا
(O Banū Asad, if only you knew our valour when the day with stars (by day) is most hideous.)
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿تَدْعُونَهُ تَضَرُّعاً وَخُفْيَةً﴾.
That is: you show humble supplication (taḍarruʿ) — which is the most extreme neediness for a thing and need of it — ﴿وَخُفْيَةً﴾, i.e. and you conceal the like of it inwardly.
So Allah commanded the Prophet ﷺ to rebuke them, since they called upon Allah, Blessed and Exalted is He, in hardships, and then outside hardships they called upon idols along with Him, which neither harm nor benefit.

nahhas-meani:65-65.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ هُوَ ٱلْقَادِرُ عَلَىٰ أَن يَبْعَثَ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَاباً مِّن فَوْقِكُمْ أَوْ مِن تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِكُمْ﴾.
ʿĀmir ibn ʿAbd Allāh said: Ibn ʿAbbās used to say: As for the punishment ﴿مِّن فَوْقِكُمْ﴾, it is evil leaders; and as for the punishment ﴿مِن تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِكُمْ﴾, it is evil servants. [Translator's note: «فخذم» is so in the source, for «فخَدَم» (servants).]
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: ﴿مِّن فَوْقِكُمْ﴾ means from your great ones, ﴿أَوْ مِن تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِكُمْ﴾ from your lowly ones.
Abū al-ʿAbbās said: ﴿مِّن فَوْقِكُمْ﴾ means stoning (from the sky), ﴿أَوْ مِن تَحْتِ أَرْجُلِكُمْ﴾ means the swallowing up (by the earth).
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَوْ يَلْبِسَكُمْ شِيَعاً﴾.
الشِّيَعُ are factions.
The meaning is: in factions divided, disagreeing, not in accord; and لَبَسْتُ means "I mixed up". What makes it clear is His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَيُذِيقَ بَعْضَكُمْ بَأْسَ بَعْضٍ﴾.
Ibn Abī Najīḥ said, from Mujāhid: He means civil strife and disagreement.

nahhas-meani:66-66.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَذَّبَ بِهِ قَوْمُكَ وَهُوَ ٱلْحَقُّ قُل لَّسْتُ عَلَيْكُمْ بِوَكِيلٍ﴾.
This was before he was commanded to fight, i.e. I am not fighting you until you believe; that is, I am not in the position of one put in charge of you until you believe.

nahhas-meani:67-67.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لِّكُلِّ نَبَإٍ مُّسْتَقَرٌّ وَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ﴾.
This is a threat, either of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection or of the command to fight.

nahhas-meani:68-68.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإِذَا رَأَيْتَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَخُوضُونَ فِيۤ آيَاتِنَا فَأَعْرِضْ عَنْهُمْ حَتَّىٰ يَخُوضُواْ فِي حَدِيثٍ غَيْرِهِ﴾.
Shibl related from Ibn Najīḥ from Mujāhid, who said: They are those who mock the Book of Allah. Allah forbade him to sit with them unless he forgets; then when he remembers, he should get up. He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿فَلاَ تَقْعُدْ بَعْدَ ٱلذِّكْرَىٰ مَعَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّالِمِينَ﴾.
Warqāʾ related from Ibn Najīḥ from Mujāhid, who said: They are those who say about the Qurʾān what is not true.

nahhas-meani:69-69.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَا عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يَتَّقُونَ مِنْ حِسَابِهِم مِّن شَيْءٍ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, if they sat (with them) — but they do not sit.
That is, because Allah has forbidden them.

nahhas-meani:70-70.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَذَرِ الَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ دِينَهُمْ لَعِباً وَلَهْواً، وَغَرَّتْهُمُ ٱلْحَيَاةُ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
Qatāda said: This is abrogated; it was abrogated by His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَاقْتُلُوا المُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وَجَدْتُمُوْهُمْ﴾.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَذَكِّرْ بِهِ أَن تُبْسَلَ نَفْسٌ بِمَا كَسَبَتْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: (تُبْسَلَ means) is handed over.
Al-Kisāʾī and al-Akhfash said: That is, is requited.
Al-Farrāʾ said: That is, is held in pledge.
These meanings are close to one another, and Mujāhid's statement is good, i.e. it is handed over for its deeds, unable to free itself; because one says استبسل فلان للموت, i.e. he saw what he could not ward off. And there is recited:
وَإِبْسَالِي بَنِيَّ بِغَيْرِ جُرْمٍ * بَعَوْنَاهُ وَلاَ بِدَمٍ مُرَاقِ
(And my handing over my sons, without any crime we had committed, nor for any blood that was shed.)
[Abū Jaʿfar said: بَعَوْنَاه means "we committed it".]
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِن تَعْدِلْ كُلَّ عَدْلٍ لاَّ يُؤْخَذْ مِنْهَآ﴾.
Qatāda said: العدلُ is the ransom; and we have explained it earlier.

nahhas-meani:71-71.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ أَنَدْعُواْ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ مَا لاَ يَنفَعُنَا وَلاَ يَضُرُّنَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the idols.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَنُرَدُّ عَلَىٰ أَعْقَابِنَا بَعْدَ إِذْ هَدَانَا ٱللَّهُ﴾.
That is: back to disbelief.
Abū ʿUbayda said: It is said of one who has been turned back from his aim and did not attain it: "He has been turned back on his heels."
Abū al-ʿAbbās Muḥammad ibn Yazīd said: Its meaning is: he is followed by evil after good. Its origin is from العاقبة and العُقبى, which are what comes after a thing, hoping that it will follow it. From it is ﴿وَالعَاقِبَةُ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾; from it is عَقِبُ الرجل (a man's posterity); and from it is العقوبةُ (punishment), because it follows the sin and results from it.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كَٱلَّذِي ٱسْتَهْوَتْهُ ٱلشَّيَاطِينُ فِي ٱلأَرْضِ حَيْرَانَ﴾.
The meaning of استهوته is: they made his desire (هواه) seem fair to him.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لَهُ أَصْحَابٌ يَدْعُونَهُ إِلَى ٱلْهُدَى ٱئْتِنَا﴾.
[Translator's note: the source gives no comment after this quotation.]

nahhas-meani:73-73.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ بِٱلْحَقِّ وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ كُن فَيَكُونُ﴾.
The meaning is: fear the day on which He says "Be", and it is. It is also possible that it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to His saying: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾.
If it is asked: what is the meaning of "and He created the day on which He says 'Be', and it is"?
The answer is that whatever Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, has told will come to be is equivalent to what has already been. It is also possible that the meaning is "and remind (them of the day)", and this is the best of the answers, because after it comes ﴿وإذْ قَاَلَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ﴾. [Translator's note: the source has «وذكروا»; «واذكُروا» ("and remember") or «وذَكِّروا» seems intended.]
It has also been said: the meaning is "and on the day He says 'Be' to the trumpet (al-ṣūr), it is."
It has also been said: the meaning is "then there comes to be what He wills of the death of all creatures and their resurrection."
On these two answers the complete stop (al-tamām) is at His saying ﴿فَيَكُونُ﴾.
It has also been said: the meaning is "then His word is", i.e. what He commands comes to be; and on this view the complete stop is at ﴿فَيَكُونُ قَوْلُهُ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: الصُّور is the plural of صورة (form); and this view is among those refuted against him, because ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: الصُّورُ is a horn.
In the ḥadīth from the Prophet ﷺ, he said:
"The one in charge of the trumpet has not ceased holding it to his mouth since Allah created him, waiting for when he will be commanded to blow into it."
ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd said: ʿIyāḍ read ﴿يَوْمَ يُنْفَخُ فِي الصُّوَرِ﴾, and by this he means the creatures (i.e. their forms); and Allah knows best.

nahhas-meani:74-74.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَاهِيمُ لأَبِيهِ آزَرَ أَتَتَّخِذُ أَصْنَاماً آلِهَةً﴾? [verse 74].
Al-Ḥasan read "آزَرُ" in the nominative.
In the codex (ḥarf) of Ubayy: يا آزرُ (O Āzar).
Al-Ḥasan said: It is the name of his father; and al-Ḥasan held that it is a vocative (nidāʾ).
Sulaymān al-Taymī said: The meaning of آزرُ is "O crooked one!"
It has also been said: his father had two names; he was called Tāriḥ and Āzar.
It has also been said: Āzar is the name of an idol, and the meaning on this view is: "Do you take Āzar (as god)?", i.e. "Do you take idols?!"

nahhas-meani:75-75.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ نُرِيۤ إِبْرَاهِيمَ مَلَكُوتَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ﴾.
ملكُوت in the language has the meaning of مُلْك (dominion), except that it contains a sense of intensiveness.
Sufyān related from Ibn Abī Najīḥ from Mujāhid, who said: He means the signs.
Ibn Jurayj related from al-Qāsim from Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī, who said: The seven heavens were opened for him, and he looked at them until (his sight) reached the Throne; and the earths were opened for him, and he looked at them.

nahhas-meani:76-76.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَلَمَّا جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلْلَّيْلُ﴾.
جنَّ عليه and أَجنَّه: when it covered him with its darkness. [Translator's note: the source writes «أجنّة».]
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿رَأَى كَوْكَباً﴾.
Qatāda said: We used to be told that it was Venus.
Al-Suddī said: It was Jupiter.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿هَـٰذَا رَبِّي﴾.
There are (several) answers on this:
Quṭrub said: It may be by way of a question.
This is a mistake, because a question is made only with a particle, or with (أم) occurring in the speech.
Some of the people of speculative reasoning said: He only said this to them before he received revelation. The holder of this view adduced as evidence His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿لَئِنْ لَمْ يَهْدِنِي رَبِّي لأَكُونَنَّ مِنَ القَوْمِ الضَّالِّينَ﴾.
Abū Isḥāq said: This answer is, in my view, a mistake and an error on the part of whoever said it.
Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, has told of Ibrāhīm that he said: ﴿وَاجْنُبني وَبَنيَّ أَنْ نَعْبُدَ الأَصْنَامَ﴾.
And He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿بقلب سليم﴾, i.e. he never associated partners (with Allah) at all.
He said: The answer in my view is that he said "This is my Lord" according to your claim, because they used to worship idols, the sun and the moon. The parallel of this is the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, ﴿أين شركائي﴾ — while He, Majestic and Mighty is He, has no partner — the meaning being: where are My partners, according to your claim?
It is also possible that the meaning is: "When the night covered him he saw a star — (and) they say: 'This is my Lord'", then the verb of saying was omitted, as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿والمَلاَئِكَةُ يَدْخُلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ كُلِّ بَابٍ سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾, where He omitted the verb of saying.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَلَمَّآ أَفَلَ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, it went away.
Al-Kisāʾī said: One says أَفَلَ النجم أفولاً when it sets.

nahhas-meani:77-77.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَلَمَّآ رَأَى ٱلْقَمَرَ بَازِغاً﴾.
One says بَزَغ القمرُ when the moon begins to rise.

nahhas-meani:79-79.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنِّي وَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِيَ لِلَّذِي فَطَرَ ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ حَنِيفاً﴾.
فَطَر means created; and الحنيفُ is the one inclining wholly towards Islam.

nahhas-meani:80-80.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَحَآجَّهُ قَوْمُهُ﴾.
The meaning is: and his people disputed with him, i.e. about the oneness of Allah.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ أَخَافُ مَا تُشْرِكُونَ بِهِ إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ رَبِّي شَيْئاً﴾.
The meaning is: unless my Lord wills that something should befall me because of a sin I committed; and this is an exception not of the same kind as the first (i.e. a disjoined exception).

nahhas-meani:81-81.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَأَيُّ ٱلْفَرِيقَيْنِ أَحَقُّ بِٱلأَمْنِ﴾? [verse 81].
The meaning is: is the believer more entitled to security, or the idolater?

nahhas-meani:82-82.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَلَمْ يَلْبِسُوۤاْ إِيمَانَهُمْ بِظُلْمٍ﴾.
It is possible that this is a report about Ibrāhīm ﷺ, that he said it.
It is also possible that it is a new statement (mustaʾnaf) from the speech of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He.
In some narrations from Mujāhid there is what indicates that it is a report about Ibrāhīm.
It is related from Mujāhid that he said regarding the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, ﴿وَتِلْكَ حُجَّتُنَا آتَيْنَاهَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ عَلَى قَوْمِهِ﴾: It is his saying: ﴿فَأَيُّ الفَرِيقَيْنِ أَحَقُّ بِالأَمْنِ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ تَعْلَمُونَ؟ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَلَمْ يَلْبِسُوۤاْ إِيمَانَهُمْ بِظُلْمٍ﴾.
Abū Bakr and ʿAlī — may Allah be pleased with them both — Salmān and Ḥudhayfa said regarding His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿وَلَمْ يَلْبِسُوۤاْ إِيمَانَهُمْ بِظُلْمٍ﴾: that is, with idolatry (shirk).
ʿAlqama related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: When ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَلَمْ يَلْبِسُوۤاْ إِيمَانَهُمْ بِظُلْمٍ﴾ was revealed, that weighed heavily on the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they said: "Which of us does not do wrong?!" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "It is not as you think; it is only as Luqmān said: ﴿إنّ الشّرك لظلم عظيم﴾."

nahhas-meani:84-84.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِهِ دَاوُودَ وَسُلَيْمَانَ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is "and We guided Dāwūd and Sulaymān", it being conjoined (maʿṭūf) to (كل) (i.e. كُلّاً هَدَيْنَا).
It is also possible that the meaning is: and We granted him Dāwūd and Sulaymān.

nahhas-meani:87-87.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱجْتَبَيْنَاهُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: We made them sincere (or: singled them out purely for Ourselves).
According to the philologists it has the meaning "We chose them".

nahhas-meani:89-89.t:
And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿فَإِن يَكْفُرْ بِهَا هَـٰؤُلاۤءِ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the people of Mecca.
Qatāda said: He means the people of Muḥammad, upon him be peace.
﴿فَقَدْ وَكَّلْنَا بِهَا قَوْماً لَّيْسُواْ بِهَا بِكَافِرِينَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the people of Medina.
Qatāda said: He means the prophets whose stories Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, has told.
This view is closer to the meaning, because He said afterwards: ﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ هَدَى اللَّهُ فَبِهُدَاهُمُ اقْتَدِهْ﴾.
Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to me, he said: Ibrāhīm narrated to us: ʿUthmān al-Muʾadhdhin narrated to us, from ʿAwf, from Abū Rajāʾ, concerning the saying of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَقَدْ وَكَّلْنَا بِهَا قَوْمَاً لَّيْسُواْ بِهَا بِكَافِرِينَ﴾ — he said: They are the angels.

nahhas-meani:91-91.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ﴾.
Abū ʿUbayda said: That is, they did not know Allah with the knowledge due to Him.
This is a good statement, because the meaning of قدرتُ الشيءَ and قدّرتُه is: I knew its measure.
What indicates it is His saying, Majestic and Exalted is He: ﴿إِذْ قَالُواْ مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ بَشَرٍ مِّن شَيْءٍ﴾, i.e. they did not know Him with the knowledge due to Him, since they denied that He would send a messenger.
Someone other than Abū ʿUbayda said: The meaning is: and they did not magnify Allah with the magnification due to Him. From this is (the expression) "So-and-so has standing (قَدْر)".
The two meanings are close to one another.
It is related that this was revealed about one of the Jews who used to display devotion while living in luxury in private. It was said to him: "In the Book (it says) that Allah does not love the fat rabbi", and he said: ﴿مَآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ بَشَرٍ مِّن شَيْءٍ﴾.

nahhas-meani:92-92.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلِتُنذِرَ أُمَّ ٱلْقُرَىٰ وَمَنْ حَوْلَهَا﴾.
The meaning is: and so that you may warn the people of the Mother of Towns.
Qatāda said: We used to be told that it is Mecca, because the earth was spread out from it.
It has also been said: it was called the Mother of Towns only because it is sought out from every town.

nahhas-meani:93-93.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنِ ٱفْتَرَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ كَذِباً أَوْ قَالَ أُوْحِيَ إِلَيَّ وَلَمْ يُوحَ إِلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ وَمَن قَالَ سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنَزلَ ٱللَّهُ﴾? [verse 93].
Qatāda said: It has reached us that this was revealed about Musaylima.
Abū Isḥāq said: This is a reply to their saying: ﴿لَوْ نَشَاءُ لَقُلْنَا مِثْلَ هَذَا﴾.
It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: The one who fabricated a lie against Allah is "Musaylima", and the one who said ﴿سَأُنزِلُ مِثْلَ مَآ أَنَزلَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ is "ʿAbd Allāh ibn Saʿd ibn Abī Sarḥ".
Ḥafṣ ibn ʿUmar related from al-Ḥakam ibn Abān from ʿIkrima that this verse was revealed about al-Naḍr ibn al-Ḥārith, because he tried to imitate the Qurʾān, saying: "By those that grind a grinding, and those that knead a kneading, and those that bake a baking, and those that take morsels a morsel-taking."
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَوْ تَرَىۤ إِذِ ٱلظَّالِمُونَ فِي غَمَرَاتِ ٱلْمَوْتِ﴾, i.e. its agonies, ﴿وَٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةُ بَاسِطُوۤاْ أَيْدِيهِمْ﴾.
