That is: stretching out their hands with punishment.

nahhas-meani:94-94.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, your mutual bond (i.e. reading بَيْنُكُمْ in the nominative, بَيْن meaning "bond"). [Translator's note: the verse as quoted in the source is vocalised بَيْنَكُمْ; Mujāhid's explanation corresponds to the nominative reading.]
Whoever reads (بَيْنَكُمْ) (in the accusative), the meaning is: the matter between you has been cut off.

nahhas-meani:95-95.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ فَالِقُ ٱلْحَبِّ وَٱلنَّوَىٰ﴾.
Mujāhid said: He means the split in them.
Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: فالقُ means Creator.

nahhas-meani:96-96.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَالِقُ ٱلإِصْبَاحِ﴾.
It is also read (الأَصْبَاحَ), and al-Ḥasan and ʿĪsā read it so; it is the plural of صُبْح. And الإِصباح is (a maṣdar) as you say الإِمْساءُ (evening).
Al-Nakhaʿī read ﴿فَلَقَ الإِصْبَاحَ﴾.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَجَاعِلُ ٱلْلَّيْلِ سَكَناً وَٱلشَّمْسَ وَٱلْقَمَرَ حُسْبَاناً﴾.
الحسبانُ and الحسابُ are one, i.e. possessing a reckoning, meaning their revolving.
Ibn ʿAbbās said regarding His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He, ﴿الشَّمْسُ وَالقَمَرُ بِحُسْبَانٍ﴾: that is, by reckoning.

nahhas-meani:98-98.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنشَأَكُم مِّن نَّفْسٍ وَاحِدَةٍ فَمُسْتَقَرٌّ وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ﴾.
ʿAṭāʾ, Mujāhid, Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk said — and their wordings are close to one another —: "One settled (مستقِرٌ) in the womb, and one deposited (مستودَعٌ) in the loins."
A group read it with fatḥa (مُسْتَقَرٌّ).
It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he said: المستقرُّ is the womb, and المستودعُ is the land in which one dies.
The fatḥa is in the sense of: and you have in the wombs a place of settlement, and in the loins a place of deposit.
The kasra is in the sense of: and of you there is one who is settled.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: Ibn ʿAbbās said (to me): "Have you married?" I said: "No." He said: "Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, will bring forth from your back what He has deposited in it."
Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and others read ﴿فَمُسْتَقِرٌ﴾ with kasra, and ﴿ومُسْتَوْدَعٌ﴾.
Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī said: The meaning is: one settled in the womb and one deposited in the loins. [Translator's note: the source spells the name «النّخغيّ».]
Al-Ḥasan said: One settled in the grave, and one deposited in this world, soon to join his companion.
Muḥammad ibn Idrīs narrated to me, he said: Ibrāhīm ibn Marzūq narrated to us, he said: Abū Dāwūd narrated to us, from Hushaym, from Abū Bishr, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, concerning His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ فَمُسْتَقِرٌ وَمُسْتَوْدَعٌ﴾ — he said: المستقِرٌ is what is in the womb, and المستودعُ is the loins.
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَدْ فَصَّلْنَا ٱلآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَفْقَهُونَ﴾.
Qatāda said: فصَّلنا has the meaning "We have made clear".

nahhas-meani:99-99.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءً فَأَخْرَجْنَا بِهِ نَبَاتَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ فَأَخْرَجْنَا مِنْهُ خَضِراً﴾.
﴿خَضِراً﴾ has the meaning أخضر (green).
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّخْلِ مِن طَلْعِهَا قِنْوَانٌ دَانِيَةٌ﴾.
Qatāda said: القنوانُ are the date-clusters (العُذُوق), and so it is according to most philologists.
One says عِذْقٌ and قِنْوٌ with one meaning; as for العَذق, it is the palm tree. [Translator's note: the source vocalises it «العِذق»; the word meaning "palm tree" is usually given as «العَذْق» with fatḥa.]
It has also been said: القِنْوانُ is the palm-pith (الجُمَّار).
Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib said: دانيةٌ means near.
The meaning is: and among them are distant clusters (too) — (left unmentioned) as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿سَرَابِيلَ تَقِيكُمُ الحَرَّ﴾.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَٱلزَّيْتُونَ وَٱلرُّمَّانَ مُشْتَبِهاً وَغَيْرَ مُتَشَابِهٍ﴾. [verse 99].
[That is: alike in appearance, and not alike in taste.]
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱنْظُرُوۤاْ إِلِىٰ ثَمَرِهِ إِذَآ أَثْمَرَ وَيَنْعِهِ﴾.
That is: and its ripening.
One says يَنْعٌ and يُنْعٌ, and أَيْنَعَ and يَنَع, when (fruit) ripens and matures.
Al-Ḥajjāj said in his sermon: "I see heads that have ripened and whose time for plucking has come."

nahhas-meani:100-100.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَجَعَلُواْ للَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ ٱلْجِنَّ﴾.
It has been said: its meaning is that they obeyed them as Allah is obeyed.
It has also been said: its meaning is that they attributed to them the acts that belong only to Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He; i.e. so how can a created thing, which was not and then came to be, be a partner of Allah?
* And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَخَلَقَهُمْ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is "and He created the partners", and it is possible that the meaning is "and He created those who made (them partners)".
Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar read (وخَلْقَهُم) with sukūn on the lām. He said: Its meaning is: and they made what He created (خَلْقَهم) partners to Allah.
Al-Ḥasan was asked about the meaning of (وَخَرَّقُوا لَهُ بَنِينَ وَبَنَاتٍ) with the doubled form, and he said: It is only ﴿وَخَرَقُواْ﴾ with the light form; it is an Arabic word: when a man lied in the assembly, it was said: "He has fabricated it (خَرَقها), by the Lord of the Kaʿba!"
The philologists said: the meaning of "خَرَقوا" is "they fabricated and invented", and "خَرَّقوا" expresses multiplicity (takthīr). [Translator's note: the source has «اختلَفُوا», which in this context presumably stands for «اختلَقُوا» ("they fabricated").]

nahhas-meani:101-101.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَنَّىٰ يَكُونُ لَهُ وَلَدٌ وَلَمْ تَكُنْ لَّهُ صَاحِبَةٌ﴾.
That is: whence could He have a child, when a child can only come from a consort?
﴿وَخَلَقَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ﴾, i.e. so nothing is like Him; how then could He have a child?

nahhas-meani:103-103.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لاَّ تُدْرِكُهُ ٱلأَبْصَارُ﴾.
It has been said: its meaning is: in this world.
Al-Zajjāj said: That is, the essence of His reality is not attained — as you say "I grasped (أدركتُ) such-and-such" — because the ḥadīths concerning the seeing (of Allah) on the Day of Resurrection are authentically reported from the Prophet ﷺ.

nahhas-meani:104-104.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَدْ جَآءَكُمْ بَصَآئِرُ مِن رَّبِّكُمْ فَمَنْ أَبْصَرَ فَلِنَفْسِهِ﴾.
The meaning is: the benefit of that is for himself.
﴿وَمَنْ عَمِيَ فَعَلَيْهَا﴾, i.e. the harm of that is upon it (his soul).

nahhas-meani:105-105.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ نُصَرِّفُ ٱلآيَاتِ وَلِيَقُولُواْ دَرَسْتَ﴾.
This is the reading of the people of Medina, the people of Kufa and Ibn al-Zubayr, and its meaning is: you have recited and read.
ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib read ﴿دَارَسْتَ﴾, and this is the sound (report) of the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, Mujāhid, ʿIkrima, Abū ʿAmr and the people of Mecca.
Ibn ʿAbbās said: The meaning of دارَسْتَ is: you have recited with (others) in turn.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said: That is, you have studied with the People of the Book.
Qatāda read ﴿دُرِسَتْ﴾, i.e. it has been read.
Al-Ḥasan read ﴿دَرَسَتْ﴾, i.e. it has become effaced and old.
Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna related from ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd from al-Ḥasan that he read ﴿دَارَسَتْ﴾.
Abū Ḥātim held that this reading is not permissible; he said: because the verses do not study.
Others said: reading it so is permissible, and the meaning is not what Abū Ḥātim took it to be; rather its meaning is "your community has studied", i.e. your community has studied with you. And even if there has been no prior mention of it (the community), it is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿حتَّى تَوَارَتْ بِالحِجَابِ﴾ (where the referent of the pronoun is not mentioned).
Al-Akhfash reported (the reading) (وَلِيَقُولُوا دَرُسَتْ), which has the meaning of دَرَسَتْ, except that it is more intensive.
Abū al-ʿAbbās reported that it is read (وَلْيَقُولُوا دَرَسْتَ) with sukūn on the lām, as an imperative, and it carries a sense of threat, i.e. let them say what they like, for the truth is clear — as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿فَلْيَضْحَكُوا قَلِيَلاً، وَلْيَبْكُوا كَثِيراً﴾.
As for whoever gives the lām a kasra, for him it is the lām of "kay" (purpose).
Abū Isḥāq said: The philologists call it the lām of outcome (lām al-ṣayrūra), i.e. it came to this, as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿رَبَّنَا لِيُضِلُّوا عَنْ سَبِيلِكَ﴾, and as you say: "So-and-so wrote this letter to his own death", i.e. his affair came to that.
The derivation of all these readings goes back to one thing: softening and making tractable.
دَرَسْتُ means "I read" and "I made tractable"; دَرَسَتِ الدارُ means "the dwelling became humbled and effaced"; and دَرَسَ الحنطة means "he threshed the wheat".

nahhas-meani:107-107.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مَآ أَشْرَكُواْ﴾.
It has been said: its meaning is "had Allah willed, He would have uprooted them"; and Allah knows best what He intended.
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَاكَ عَلَيْهِمْ حَفِيظاً وَمَآ أَنتَ عَلَيْهِم بِوَكِيلٍ﴾.
This was before he was commanded to fight.

nahhas-meani:108-108.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَسُبُّواْ ٱلَّذِينَ يَدْعُونَ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ فَيَسُبُّواْ ٱللَّهَ عَدْواً بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ﴾.
Qatāda said: The Muslims used to revile the idols, and the idolaters would revile Allah in hostility (عَدْواً), without knowledge.
It is related that in the reading of the people of Mecca it is (عَدُوّاً بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ), and the reading is good; "عَدُوَّاً" has the meaning of "enemies", as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿إِنَّ الكَافِرِينَ كَانُوا لَكُمْ عَدُوَّاً مُبِينَاً﴾. [Translator's note: the source has «جسنة», a misprint for «حسنة».]
It is also read (عُدُوَّاً). One says, when someone exceeds the bounds in wrongdoing: عَدَا يَعْدُو، عَدْواً، وعُدُوَّاً، وعُدْواناً، وعَدَاءً.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كَذَلِكَ زَيَّنَّا لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ عَمَلَهُمْ﴾.
It has been said: its meaning is (that it was) a requital for their disbelief.
It has also been said: "their deeds" means the deeds they ought to do, namely faith and obedience; and Allah knows best the reality of that.

nahhas-meani:109-109.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَأَقْسَمُواْ بِٱللَّهِ جَهْدَ أَيْمَانِهِمْ﴾.
That is: they exerted themselves in swearing ﴿لَئِن جَآءَتْهُمْ آيَةٌ لَّيُؤْمِنُنَّ بِهَا﴾.
They meant a sign of the kind they were demanding.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَا يُشْعِرُكُمْ أَنَّهَآ إِذَا جَآءَتْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The meaning is: and what makes you know? He said: Then He began anew and said: ﴿إِنَّهَا إِذَا جَاءَتْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.
The people of Medina read: ﴿أَنَّهَآ إِذَا جَآءَتْ﴾.
Al-Kisāʾī said: (لا) here is redundant (zāʾida), and the meaning is: and what makes you know that, when it comes, they will believe?
And he likened it to His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَلاَّ تَسْجُدَ إِذْ أَمَرْتُكَ﴾?
This, according to the Basrans, is a mistake, because (لا) is not redundant in a position where it can be negative.
Al-Khalīl said: The meaning is لعلَّها ("perhaps it…"), and he likened it to the Arabs' saying: إيتِ السُّوقَ أَنّك تشتري لنا شيئاً ("Go to the market; perhaps you will buy us something"), in the sense of لعلَّك.
It is related that in the reading of Ubayy it is: ﴿وَمَا يُشْعِرُكُمْ لَعَلَّهَا إِذَا جَاءَتْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾?!
The philologists recited, for (أَنَّ) in the sense of (لعلَّ):
أَريني جَواداً مَاتَ هُزْلاً لأَنَّنِي * أَرَى ما تَرَيْنَ أو بَخَيِلاً مُخَلَّدَا
(Show me a generous man who died of leanness — perhaps I see what you see — or a miser made immortal.)
It has also been said: there is an omission in the statement, and the meaning is: and what makes you know whether, when it comes, they will not believe or will believe? Then this was omitted because the hearer knows it.
It is related that the idolaters said: "Ask Allah to send down upon us the sign about which He said ﴿إِنْ نَشَأْ نُنَزِّلْ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ آيَةً فَظَلَّتْ أَعْنَاقُهُمْ لَهَا خَاضِعِينَ﴾, and we — by Allah — will believe." The Muslims said: "O Messenger of Allah, ask Allah to send it down!" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed ﴿وَمَا يُشْعِرُكُمْ أَنَّهَآ إِذَا جَآءَتْ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.

nahhas-meani:110-110.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَنُقَلِّبُ أَفْئِدَتَهُمْ وَأَبْصَارَهُمْ﴾.
"أفئدةٌ" is the plural of فؤاد (heart).

nahhas-meani:111-111.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّنَا نَزَّلْنَآ إِلَيْهِمُ ٱلْمَلاۤئِكَةَ وَكَلَّمَهُمُ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ وَحَشَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ قُبُلاً مَّا كَانُواْ لِيُؤْمِنُوۤاْ إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
It is related that they asked for these things, and this was revealed.
Mujāhid said: ﴿قُبُلاً﴾ means in throngs, i.e. group by group.
He holds that it is the plural of قبيل, which is a party.
It has also been said: it is the plural of قبيل, and "قبيلٌ" has the meaning of a guarantor, i.e. even if the angels and others guaranteed to them the truth of this, they would not believe — as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿أَوْ تَأْتِيَ بِاللَّهِ وَالمَلائِكَةِ قَبِيَلاً﴾.
It is also possible that the meaning of ﴿قُبُلاً﴾ is like the meaning of "face to face", as He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿إِنْ كَانَ قَمِيصُهُ قُدَّ مِنْ قُبُلٍ﴾.
Whoever reads (قِبَلاً), its meaning for him is: seeing it with their own eyes.

nahhas-meani:112-112.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ جَعَلْنَا لِكُلِّ نِبِيٍّ عَدُوّاً﴾.
That is: just as We have made for you and your community enemies; and عدوٌّ has the meaning of أعداء (enemies).
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿شَيَاطِينَ ٱلإِنْسِ وَٱلْجِنِّ﴾.
Al-Aʿmash read ﴿شَيَاطِينَ الجِنِّ وَالإِنْسِ﴾, and the meaning is the same.
Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿يُوحِي بَعْضُهُمْ إِلَىٰ بَعْضٍ زُخْرُفَ ٱلْقَوْلِ غُرُوراً﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, they make that seem fair to them, i.e. they make ugly deeds seem fair to them.
Likewise الزخرف in the language is adornment, and from it gold is called زخرف.
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلَوْ شَآءَ رَبُّكَ مَا فَعَلُوهُ فَذَرْهُمْ وَمَا يَفْتَرُونَ﴾.
That is: had He willed, He would have prevented them from whispering to human beings; but He tests with what He wills, in order to make the reward abundant.

nahhas-meani:113-113.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلِتَصْغَىۤ إِلَيْهِ أَفْئِدَةُ ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱلآخِرَةِ﴾.
One says صَغَى يَصْغَى, صَغَا يَصْغُو and أَصْغَى يُصْغِي when (something) inclines, as the poet said:
تُصْغِي إِذَا شَدَّهَا بِالرَّحْل جَانِحَةً * حَتَّى إذَا ما اسْتَوَى فِي غَرْزِهَا تَثِبُ
(She leans over, bending, when he binds the saddle on her; then, when he is settled in her stirrup, she leaps forward.)
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَلِيَرْضَوْهُ وَلِيَقْتَرِفُواْ مَا هُم مُّقْتَرِفُونَ﴾.
That is: and so that they may earn. One says قرفتُ الجلدَ when you have peeled off the skin (or scab).
It is also read (وَلْيَقْتَرفُوا) (with sukūn, as an imperative), and it carries a sense of threat.
Qatāda said: Truthful in what He promised, and just in what He decreed. [Translator's note: so in the source; this comment explains «صِدْقاً وَعَدْلاً» in verse 115, which is not quoted here.]

nahhas-meani:116-116.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلاَّ ٱلظَّنَّ﴾.
He, Majestic and Mighty is He, made known that they are not upon clear insight or certainty, and that they do not follow the truth.
It is also read ﴿إِنَ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعْلَمُ مَنْ يُضِلُّ عَنْ سَبِيِلهِ﴾ (i.e. يُضِلُّ, "who leads astray").
This is on the basis of omission of the object (mafʿūl bihi), and the fatḥa on the yāʾ (يَضِلُّ, "who goes astray") is better, because after it comes: ﴿وَهُو أَعْلَمُ بِالمُهْتَدِينَ﴾. [Translator's note: this discussion concerns verse 117, whose text is quoted here; «إِنَ» is so in the source.]

nahhas-meani:118-118.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَكُلُواْ مِمَّا ذُكِرَ ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾.
That is: of what has been dedicated purely to Allah; and the prohibition of carrion is included in this.

nahhas-meani:119-119.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَا لَكُمْ أَلاَّ تَأْكُلُواْ مِمَّا ذُكِرَ ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾.
ʿIkrima related from Ibn ʿAbbās that the idolaters said to the Muslims: "Why do you eat what you have killed, and not eat what Allah has killed for you?" So Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, revealed: ﴿وَإِنَّ الشَّيَاطِينَ لَيُوحُونَ إِلَى أَوْلِيَائِهِمْ لِيُجَادِلُوكُمْ﴾.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَقَدْ فَصَّلَ لَكُمْ مَّا حَرَّمَ عَلَيْكُمْ إِلاَّ مَا ٱضْطُرِرْتُمْ إِلَيْهِ﴾.
Qatāda said: فصَّل means "made clear".
ʿAṭiyya al-ʿAwfī read (وَقَدْ فَصَلَ لَكُمْ) with the light form. [Translator's note: the source has «خفية», evidently for «خفيفة» ("light", i.e. without doubling).]
Its meaning is: became clear and manifest, as was read (آلر. كِتَابٌ أُحْكِمَتْ آيَاتُهُ ثُمَّ فَصَلَتْ), i.e. became clear.

nahhas-meani:120-120.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَذَرُواْ ظَاهِرَ ٱلإِثْمِ وَبَاطِنَهُ﴾.
Qatāda said: That is, its open and its secret (forms).
Someone else said: the outward sin is "fornication", and the inward is "taking secret lovers".
Closer to the language is the statement of Qatāda.
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكْسِبُونَ ٱلإِثْمَ سَيُجْزَوْنَ بِمَا كَانُواْ يَقْتَرِفُونَ﴾.
That is: they earn and do. One says قرفتُ الجلدَ, i.e. I peeled it off.
Abū Jaʿfar said: The scholars differed about the meaning of ﴿وَلاَ تَأْكُلُوا مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾. The position of Ibn ʿAbbās was that this is a reply to the idolaters when they questioned the Prophet ﷺ and disputed, saying: "How is it that we do not eat of what your Lord has killed, yet eat of what we have killed?" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, revealed: ﴿وَلاَ تَأْكُلُوا مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ اسْمُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿIkrima related it from him; so the meaning on this view is: and do not eat of carrion.
Al-Shaʿbī and Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn said: Slaughtered animals over which the name of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, was not mentioned are not to be eaten, whether that was deliberate or through forgetfulness.
Saʿīd ibn Jubayr and ʿAṭāʾ said: If he omitted the invocation (tasmiya) deliberately, it is not eaten; and if he forgot, it is eaten. And this is good, because one is not called a transgressor (fāsiq) if he forgot.

nahhas-meani:121-121.t:
And the meaning of ﴿وَلاَ تَأْكُلُواْ مِمَّا لَمْ يُذْكَرِ ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ﴾ is:
of what has not been dedicated purely to Allah.
﴿وَإِنَّهُ لَفِسْقٌ﴾, i.e. a departure from obedience. One says فسقت الرطبة when the ripe date comes out of its skin.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِنَّ ٱلشَّيَاطِينَ لَيُوحُونَ إِلَىۤ أَوْلِيَآئِهِمْ لِيُجَادِلُوكُمْ﴾.
That is: they whisper to them.
And I have already mentioned the meaning of "to dispute with you".
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَإِنْ أَطَعْتُمُوهُمْ إِنَّكُمْ لَمُشْرِكُونَ﴾.
The people of speculative reasoning (ahl al-naẓar) said: In this is a proof that whoever makes lawful what Allah has forbidden, or forbids what Allah has made lawful, has associated partners (with Him).
He is called an idolater (mushrik) because he followed other than Allah, and so associated something else with Him, Majestic and Mighty is He.

nahhas-meani:122-122.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿أَوَ مَن كَانَ مَيْتاً فَأَحْيَيْنَاهُ﴾.
Mujāhid said: The meaning is: or one who was astray and We guided him: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا لَهُ نُوراً يَمْشِي بِهِ فِي ٱلنَّاسِ﴾, i.e. guidance, ﴿كَمَن مَّثَلُهُ فِي ٱلظُّلُمَاتِ لَيْسَ بِخَارِجٍ مِّنْهَا﴾?
Mujāhid said: That is, in misguidance.
Al-Suddī said: This was revealed about "ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb" — Allah's mercy be upon him — and Abū Jahl.
What the meaning requires is that it be general, unless a narration about it is authentic.

nahhas-meani:123-123.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَكَذٰلِكَ جَعَلْنَا فِي كُلِّ قَرْيَةٍ أَكَابِرَ مُجَرِمِيهَا﴾.
Mujāhid said: That is, their great ones.
Someone else said: The great ones and the chiefs were singled out because they are more capable of corruption.
* Then He said, Exalted is He: ﴿وَمَا يَمْكُرُونَ إِلاَّ بِأَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾.
That is: the evil consequence of that returns upon them.

nahhas-meani:124-124.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿سَيُصِيبُ ٱلَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُواْ صَغَارٌ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ﴾.
Even if they were mighty in this world, humiliation will overtake them on the Day of Resurrection.
On the verse there are three views:
One of them is that the meaning is "humiliation will befall those who committed crimes in the sight of Allah", by way of advancing and postponing (taqdīm wa-taʾkhīr).
The second view is that the meaning is: there will befall those who committed crimes a humiliation established in the sight of Allah.
This is the best of the views, because (عند) is in its proper place.
The third view, mentioned by al-Farrāʾ, is that the meaning may be: there will befall those who committed crimes a humiliation from Allah (من عند الله).
This is a mistake according to the Basrans, because (مِنْ) is not omitted in a case like this.

nahhas-meani:125-125.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿فَمَن يُرِدِ ٱللَّهُ أَن يَهْدِيَهُ يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلإِسْلاَمِ﴾.
It is related that ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd said: "O Messenger of Allah, does the breast become expanded?!" He said: "Yes, light enters the heart." He said: "And is there a sign of that?" He ﷺ said: "Withdrawing from the abode of delusion, turning to the abode of eternity, and preparing for death before death."
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَمَن يُرِدْ أَن يُضِلَّهُ يَجْعَلْ صَدْرَهُ ضَيِّقاً حَرَجاً﴾.
That is: extremely constricted.
ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās read (ضَيْقاً حَرَجَاً).
It is related that ʿUmar summoned a Bedouin of Kināna, of Banū Mudlij, and said to him: "What is the ḥaraja?" He said: "A tree which neither wild animal nor grazing beast can reach." He said: "Such is the heart of the disbeliever: nothing of faith or good reaches it."
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّعَّدُ فِي ٱلسَّمَآءِ﴾.
Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ibn Kathīr and Shibl read: ﴿كَأَنَّما يَصْعَدُ فِي السَّمَاءِ﴾. [Translator's note: the source spells the name «ابن محيص».]
Ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān the Qurʾān-reader and Ibrāhīm al-Nakhaʿī read: ﴿كَأَنَّمَا يَصَّاعَدُ﴾. [Translator's note: so in the source; elsewhere the book names "Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān" (al-Sulamī) as the reader.]
It is related from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd that he used to read: ﴿كَأَنَّمَا يَتَصَعَّدُ﴾.
The meaning of this reading and of the reading of whoever reads يصَّعَّد and يصَّاعد is one.
The meaning in them is that the disbeliever, because of the constriction of his breast, is as if he wants to climb up into the sky while he is unable to do so — as if he is trying to bring that about.
Whoever reads "يَصْعَدُ", its meaning is that because of the constriction of his breast it is as if he were in a state of climbing that he has been burdened with.
Abū ʿUbayd said: From this is ʿUmar's saying: "No speech has been as hard on me (تصعَّدَتني) — no speech has been as hard on me as the marriage sermon."
This was objected to against Abū ʿUbayd, and it was said: this is rather from الصَّعُود, which is the arduous mountain path. Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُوداً﴾.
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كَذٰلِكَ يَجْعَلُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلرِّجْسَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ لاَ يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾.
Mujāhid said: الرِّجسُ is that in which there is no good.
Likewise الرِّجْسُ according to the philologists is stench. So the meaning of the verse — and Allah knows best — is: and He places the curse in this world and the punishment in the Hereafter upon those who do not believe.

nahhas-meani:126-126.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَدْ فَصَّلْنَا ٱلآيَاتِ لِقَوْمٍ يَذَّكَّرُونَ﴾.
That is: We have made clear.

nahhas-meani:127-127.t:
Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿لَهُمْ دَارُ ٱلسَّلاَمِ عِندَ رَبِّهِمْ﴾.
It is possible that the meaning is "the abode of safety", i.e. in which one is safe from afflictions.
It is also possible that the meaning is "the abode of Allah, Majestic and Mighty is He", for He is al-Salām.

nahhas-meani:128-128.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ يِحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعاً يَامَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ قَدِ ٱسْتَكْثَرْتُمْ مِّنَ ٱلإِنْسِ﴾.
The meaning is (in) what will be said to them: "O company of jinn, you have taken many of mankind", i.e. those whom you led astray are many.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿وَقَالَ أَوْلِيَآؤُهُم مِّنَ ٱلإِنْسِ رَبَّنَا ٱسْتَمْتَعَ بَعْضُنَا بِبَعْضٍ﴾.
There are two views on this:
One of them is that the jinn led mankind astray, and mankind accepted (it) from them.
The other view is that when a man travelled in the Jāhiliyya and was afraid, he would say: "I seek refuge with the master of this valley from the evil of what I fear"; this is mankind's enjoyment of the jinn.
And the jinn's enjoyment of mankind is that (mankind) acknowledge that the jinn are able to ward off from them what they encounter.
The first view is better, and what indicates it is ﴿يَامَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ قَدِ ٱسْتَكْثَرْتُمْ مِّنَ ٱلإِنْسِ﴾.
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قَالَ ٱلنَّارُ مَثْوَاكُمْ﴾.
المثوى is the place of abode.
* Then He said, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَآ إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
There are two views on this:
One of them is that it is an exception not of the same kind as the first (a disjoined exception), and the meaning on this view is: except what Allah wills of increase in their punishment.
Sībawayh illustrates this as having the meaning of (لكن) "but".
Al-Farrāʾ illustrates it as having the meaning of (سِوى) "besides", as you say: "I will surely house you in this house for a year, except what you wish", i.e. besides what you wish in addition. Similar to it is ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهِ مَا دَامَتِ السَّمَاوَاتُ وَالأَرْضُ إِلاَّ مَا شَاءَ رَبُّكَ﴾, i.e. besides what your Lord wills in addition.
Abū Jaʿfar said: Abū Isḥāq said: The meaning of the exception here, in my view — and Allah knows best — is only from the Day of Resurrection, i.e. except what your Lord wills of the duration of their gathering and their reckoning.
What indicates this answer is ﴿وَيَوْمَ يَحْشُرُهُمْ جَمِيعاً﴾, because by this the Day of Resurrection is meant. It is also possible that the meaning is "(except) the kinds of punishment with which Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, wills to punish them".

nahhas-meani:130-130.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿يَامَعْشَرَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَٱلإِنْسِ أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِّنْكُمْ﴾.
But the messengers are from mankind? There are two answers to this:
One of them is that it is related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: The messengers of the jinn are those who met their people and conveyed (the message) to them.
Ibn ʿAbbās means those who said: ﴿إِنَّا سَمِعْنَا قُرْآنَاً عَجَبَاً﴾. They are in the position of messengers to their people, because they conveyed (the message) to them.
Likewise Mujāhid said: The messengers are among mankind, and the warning is among the jinn.
The other view is that since mankind and jinn are both among those who are addressed and who understand, it was said "Did not messengers come to you from among you?", even though the messengers are from mankind specifically.

nahhas-meani:133-133.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿كَمَآ أَنشَأَكُمْ مِّن ذُرِّيَّةِ قَوْمٍ آخَرِينَ﴾.
الإِنشاءُ is the origination of creation.

nahhas-meani:135-135.t:
And His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿قُلْ يَاقَوْمِ ٱعْمَلُواْ عَلَىٰ مَكَانَتِكُمْ﴾.
There are two views on it:
One of them is that the meaning is: according to your capacity.
The other view is that it is as you say "Stay in your place", i.e. stay as you are.
If it is asked: how can they be commanded to stay as they are when they are disbelievers?
The answer is that this is a threat, as He, Majestic and Mighty is He, said: ﴿فَلْيَضْحَكُوا قَلِيلاً وَلْيَبْكُوا كثيراً﴾.
What indicates it is His saying ﴿فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ مَن تَكُونُ لَهُ عَاقِبَةُ ٱلدَّارِ﴾.
The meaning on this view is: stay as you are, if you are content with the Fire.
